description: The product name.
The running build's version.
The current tick index.
The clock's sample rate. Observed from the device from Phase 2; not a setting.
The audio block size the clock is being advanced by.
Samples per 50 Hz tick; the sample rate divided by 50.
How late the last tick was processed, in samples.
The worst lateness since the engine started.
Which clock is advancing the sample counter.
Commands rejected since the engine started.

Allocations Go.dot's own code made on the audio thread since the engine started. Zero is the only acceptable value: PRD 4.2 forbids allocation there, and an allocation is a lock inside the allocator taken while a block is due. Reads zero in a build configured without the real-time checks, where nobody is looking.

Allocations Tracktion made inside the audio callback since the engine started, counted separately and never hidden. Tracktion takes a shared lock every block by design; this is a measured fact about a dependency, not a defect in it.

How many ticks pass between a GO being applied and the sound starting. It is not a preference: it is one tick plus however many the audio block spans, which is the smallest delay that guarantees the launch is never placed in the past and so never back-dated. Published because a designer timing a cue against light needs the number rather than a feeling about it.

How many ticks pass between one member of an automatic sequence ending and the next one sounding. Two, plus the launch latency: a member reports it has ended during one tick, the scheduler sees that on the next and asks for the next member, and the launch is placed on the one after. It is the price of every decision being a logged command rather than something a hook quietly does - which is what lets a whole show replay - and it is published for the same reason the launch latency is: a designer timing a chain against light needs the number rather than a feeling about it. A sample-accurate join is what ranges are for (PRD 3.24); a sequence group is discrete cues relaunched.
The most recent rejection: tick, sequence, origin, reason and command. The only way an OSC client can learn that its write was refused.

How many times the edit-time liveness analysis has been rebuilt since the engine started. Published so that the cache behind it can be asserted by COUNTING rather than by timing (measurement M18): what the design guarantees is that a hundred publishes with nothing edited cost no rebuild at all, and a wall-clock threshold on a shared CI runner is a flaky test that teaches people to re-run the suite. The same argument as mountRebuilds in Phase 3, which is the shape this borrows.

Whether the tick thread - the show's clock, which every launch, fade and cursor waits on - runs at real-time priority: TIME_CRITICAL on Windows, a time-constraint policy and the interface's audio workgroup on macOS, SCHED_FIFO on Linux. False where the system refused it, typically Linux without real-time rights; the show's clock then runs at the priority of everything else on the machine.

How many times the audio interface left a gap between two calls for sound - longer than three blocks and at least 10 ms - since the engine started. Go.dot's clock is counted from those calls, so a gap is silence and a clock standing still at once. Each is also written to the engine log as a note with its length beside the longest Go.dot took to answer a call, which tells an interface that went quiet from a callback that was held up.
The longest such gap since the engine started, in samples at the session's rate.
The longest Go.dot has taken to answer one call for sound since the engine started, in samples at the session's rate. Past one block's worth, the interface was kept waiting.

Lines of the engine log made and not yet flushed to its file by the low-priority writer: what a process killed now would lose. The black-box harness waits for nought before it stops a server, since terminate() on Windows runs no destructor.
The open bundle's folder.
The open bundle's name.
The show format this document was written against.
Whether there are unsaved changes to show.xml.

How many times the show half of the document has changed since it was opened - what show.xml would record - counting from 1, so it never reads 0. A GO, a standby move, a focus change and every run leave it where it is, because none of them is a change to the show; an edit, an undo, a revert and a recovery all move it. A client rebuilds its picture of the show when this moves and not otherwise, which is the reason it exists: the document half of a snapshot is rebuilt whenever any command applies, so a chain of runs would otherwise have a cue list rebuilt several times a second for a show nobody edited. Read the difference for nothing - one move is a remove and an add - only whether it differs from the number a picture was built at.

Everything wrong with the open show that did not stop it opening, one per line: the references that point at nothing, and the slot overlaps the edit-time analysis found. NEWLINE-SEPARATED and not space-separated, which no other list-shaped readout here is, because a warning is a sentence and sentences contain spaces. A refusal is not in it - a document that fails validate is never handed to the engine, so by the time anything can read this there are none.

Show mode, and a lock on the show rather than a mode in a client. While it is true the engine refuses every change to what show.xml would record - a create, a delete, a move, or a write to any value that persists in the show - with the reason locked, whichever client sent it, because a lock that only one client honoured would lock exactly one of them - and the accident it exists for is the one PRD 3.17 names, a forearm on a screen in the dark. It locks nothing of where the operator is standing. GO, Doh!, the standby, the focus, every run, load-to-time, a save and a write to a mounted device all keep working, and so does the write that sets this false again. Kept in state.xml beside the standby and the focus rather than in show.xml, because like them it belongs to the performance in progress and not to the show - and so an engine restarted in the middle of a performance comes back locked.

Whether the document's undo history has a transaction to unmake. A client greys its Undo item from this one node and never has to send a command to find out. It is a reading of a stack that starts empty at every open, so it persists nowhere: an engine restarted mid-performance comes back with nothing to undo, which is honest - the actions are gone with the process that held them.

Whether the document has a transaction to put back. False until something has been undone, and false again the moment any edit lands, because an edit made after an undo discards the forward half - which is how every editor behaves and is the half people are surprised by.

The name of the transaction Undo would unmake, which is the command that made it: node.set, cue.create, object.delete. Published so that a menu item can read Undo object.delete rather than Undo, with no lookup table in the client - PRD 4.11 already makes every gesture-reachable action carry a name, and this is that name handed back. Empty when there is nothing to undo. It never carries a time: the engine's own notion of when is the tick index, and a wall clock in a published node would be a value a replay could not reproduce.
The same for Redo: the name of the transaction Redo would put back, and empty when nothing has been undone.

The whole of what Undo would unmake, newest first, space-separated: the name of each transaction on the document's history, which is the command that made it. Published beside undoName (2026-09-19) so a client can draw the history as a place to stand in - the author's undo panel, where a pointer dragged over the transactions shows what standing there would change - without a command to ask for it. Moving there is that many undo or redo records, each a transaction the log replays.
The same for Redo: what it would put back, nearest first, and empty when nothing has been undone.

What `document.copy` last copied: the chosen cues as one canonical <Fragment>, the text `document.paste` takes. A window puts it on the operating system's clipboard when it changes, which is how two shows in two windows hand cues to each other; the page pastes it straight back. Empty until something is copied.

What `cue.copyPart` last copied: part of one cue - its EQ, its sends, its effects, its time and loops - as a canonical <Fragment part="…">, the text `cue.pastePart` takes (namespace draft §38). Kept apart from `clipboard`, so a paste of cues is never handed a part. Empty until something is copied.

Whether an earlier session left unsaved work in this bundle that nobody has answered yet. The engine autosaves the show to recovery/ two seconds after an edit and every thirty seconds through a long one, never to show.xml - a designer who decides an afternoon was wrong must be able to throw it away by not saving. This is true when the bundle opened with a recovery/show.xml - the last session died - or, failing that, with a recovery.previous.N/ an earlier session moved aside and nobody answered, the highest N first; and it stays true until document.recover adopts that recovery or document.discardRecovery deletes it, wherever it then lives. This session's own autosave keeps running meanwhile: the first time it needs recovery/ while the offer still sits there, it renames the offer to the next recovery.previous.N/ and writes its own, so neither afternoon is lost. Nothing but a discard deletes an unanswered recovery.previous.N/, so one nobody answers is offered again at the next open; one that was recovered is deleted once the recovered work has been autosaved or saved. It is NOT a look at the disk: this session's own autosave writes recovery/ within seconds of any edit, so a node that asked the filesystem would offer every unsaved show back to the person still writing it. What it reports is somebody else's unfinished afternoon, and only the operator may decide whether it was worth keeping - the engine is headless and has nobody to ask. It changes at most twice in a session, which is why the cap is 1 and not the 5 of its livelier neighbours.

Why the last write the engine handed to its writer thread did not land, in the writer's own sentence - which command, at which tick, which file and what became of it - and empty when nothing is outstanding. Saves, autosaves, copies and discards of a recovery are written off the tick thread so that GO never waits for a disk, which means a write that fails can no longer refuse the command that asked for it: the command was applied, and its record means taken and handed to the writer. What a failure does instead is leave dirty lit, because the show on disk is still behind - the truthful signal - and say why here. NOT lastError, which quotes a refused record by tick and sequence: this failure has no such record, and counting it there would make errorCount disagree with the log. It goes out when a later write of the same command lands, or when a save lands over an autosave's failure; an autosave landing says nothing about a save that did not.

How many EQ and send changes a locked show is riding live: what the window-s bar counts while the show is unlocked, offering to keep them in the show - one undo step - or discard them (author, 2026-09-25).

Whether the live recorder is on (author, 2026-09-18: a Live recorder that records all the cue starts, to store timings triggered once by hand and then automated). record.start turns it on; from then every applied go, cue.fire and trigger.fire on any list is kept with its tick; record.stop writes them into a take - a timeline group of start cues in a list named Live recorder, each at the second it was fired - and turns it off. What it keeps is the list-s own step history, unbounded while it records: the author-s reframing that a live recorder dumps the load-to-time history to a group for replay.

The identifiers of the show's cue lists, in order, space-separated. The roster of what can be run at once: PRD 3.5 has several lists live together, each with a standby of its own, so that a timecode- or OSC-triggered chain can never move the operator's position.

Which list GO acts on. Exactly one, and exclusive by construction rather than by upkeep - it is one value, so there is no flag anywhere to leave set. A list that has gone takes the focus with it and the first remaining list has it instead, which is why nothing has to remember to move this when a list is deleted. It is remembered across a save for the same reason the standby is: a rehearsal reopened where it was left is the kinder default, and losing state.xml costs only where somebody had got to.

The least time between two GOs, in seconds (PRD 3.7-s GO debounce; a show setting since 2026-09-28, at the author-s direction). A GO pressed sooner than this after the last GO that fired something is refused as too-soon: nothing fires, the standby does not move, and the error line says a GO was eaten - so a hand that bounced, or two people on two GO buttons, cannot fire the cue after the one the operator meant. Every GO counts, from the keyboard, a surface-s PLAY or a network client; a cue fired by name or by a trigger is not a GO and is never held back. Half a second unless the show says otherwise (the author, 2026-09-28); nought is off. It also spaces two presses of Doh!, so a bounced or held Doh! is not taken for the deliberate second one.

How long after a GO, Doh! may still take it back, in seconds (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-09-30). Doh! takes back the LAST GO only - the pointer, the list-s finished flag, the GO debounce and the history go back to where that GO found them, and what it started comes down - and only while it is this recent: a press later than this is refused as too-late and the line at the foot of the window says so. Ten seconds unless the show says otherwise, nought turns Doh! off (both the implementer-s calls). Set on Show settings > Playback, right after the GO debounce, and saved with the show, so the lock refuses an edit of it as it refuses any setting.

What Doh! would take back now: the list the last GO moved, the cue it fired and the tick it fired on, space-separated - empty when there is nothing to take back (no GO yet, the last one already taken back, forgotten by a jump on its list, or a trigger fired on that list since). One for the whole engine and not one per list, because a Doh acts on the list of the last GO whichever list has the focus. What the Doh! button reads to name the cue while the GO is still inside list/dohWindow; never stored, because it is what the machine is doing (PRD 4.10).

What a press of Doh! would forget now (PRD 3.32; D2-s review, 2026-10-03): the list and the cue of the resume the last Doh! left, space-separated, when no GO a press could take back stands before it - none since, or the last one past list/dohWindow - and empty otherwise. A second press forgets that resume, and the next GO starts the cue from its top. One for the whole engine, because a press acts on the list of the last Doh! whichever list has the focus. What the Doh! button reads to offer that press, and to name the cue it would act on; never stored, because it is what the machine is doing (PRD 4.10).

What the last Doh! put back and what it left alone (PRD 3.32; D3, 2026-10-03): the list it acted on, the tick of its report and one sentence, space-separated - or the same of the relaunch of a scene that followed it, whichever came last - and empty until a Doh! has something to say. A desk value it put back, one another writer had changed since the GO, a device and the cues left to its operator, a cue it could not take back, a scene that comes back once it has ended: each in a few words, one after another. One for the whole engine, because a Doh! acts on the list of the last GO whichever list has the focus. Composed by the engine on the tick after the press; never stored, because it is what the machine is doing (PRD 4.10).
The cue list's name.
The identifiers of the list's top-level children, in order, space-separated.

The identifiers of the cues in this list's persistent section, in order, space-separated. PRD 3.29: a persistent cue is the thing that should be running at all times and is relaunched if it is not, in a section of its own - not the header, because a header fires once and never resets while a persistent cue re-asserts. The cursor skips the section as it skips a footer, standby.set refuses its cues, and they are not GO targets; after every applied go, cue.fire or trigger.fire the engine checks each one against what it declares and relaunches or re-sends through run.assert. Kinds honoured: media, osc and midi; a fade, a stop or a group in the section is a validate warning and is ignored. Empty when the list has no section.
The identifier of this list's persistent section, or empty when it has none - what cue.create takes as a parent to put a cue in it. Made by list.persistent, which answers with the one that exists.

Whether the list's persistent section is drawn shut. Recorded with the show (author, 2026-09-18: 'fold state should be recorded in project file') as state, since how a list is read is not a decision about what it plays: it lands in state.xml beside the standby and does not mark the show unsaved.

The cue GO will act on. One per list, and always one of that list's own top-level children or empty; moved only by a standby command, a write to this node, or the repair when the cue it names is deleted or moved away. Never by selection or scrolling.

Whether this list's pointer is empty because the list RAN OUT rather than because nobody has armed it. The two look identical - one empty string - and they are opposite facts about the show: a list nobody has parked on has had nothing happen to it, and a list whose last cue has been fired has had everything happen to it. Nothing needed to tell them apart until GO began clearing the pointer at the end (PRD 3.5, amended 2026-09-18); the persistent solver had been reading an empty pointer as the top of the list, so without this a show run through to its end would re-assert every persistent bed a Stop had suspended - the beds coming back on after the last cue. It goes true when a GO fires the last cue there is, false the moment anybody parks the pointer anywhere, and it is kept in state.xml beside the standby because it is the same fact about the same performance in progress. It is WRITABLE for the same reason the standby beside it is - the document's own door refuses a read-only attribute, and this is a fact about the pointer rather than a reading taken off one - but no client needs to touch it: standby.set clears it, and firing the last cue is what sets it.

Where an operator is pointing when they ask what the show WOULD be: a cue identifier and an offset in seconds, space-separated. PRD 3.13-s state position, and it is a cue and an offset rather than a wall time because a manual list has no time in it - between two GOs there is however long the actor took, so -the state at 04:12- is a question the document cannot answer. An offset of -1 means BEFORE that cue has fired: standby on it and nothing of it done, which is what -take it back to cue 12- means and is a different position from nought seconds in. Written through list.aim; read by a client dragging a finger along the list.

What the show would be at the aim, as JSON: the standby to set, the runs that should be sounding and how far into each, the values the desk should be holding and which cue last wrote each, the trims a fade left behind, and the CONFUSED list. One node holding a document rather than a subtree of nodes appearing and vanishing under a dragged finger - a solve changes shape as the aim moves, and a namespace that grew and shrank at fifty hertz would be one no client could subscribe to. The confused list is the feature rather than the apology (PRD 3.24): every place the walk could not know, with the default it took. Since 2026-09-19 it also says HOW it was read - history, when the aimed cue has a step and every cue fired before the instant is placed by the clock the steps kept, or order, the reading from the list alone - and the instant, the wall tick the plan describes, or -1 for the order.

Where the last load-to-time actually landed, in the same spelling as aim - PRD 3.13-s second pointer. After a jump the two agree; after a manual tweak they do not, and that divergence is exactly what a running view has to show, because it is the difference between where the operator asked to be and where the show has got to since.

The last sixty-four steps this list took, newest first, space-separated, each as tick:cue:origin - when, what, and whether it was a GO (g), a cue fired by name (f), a trigger (t), a press on a sampler strip (p) or a Doh! (d) - which takes the GO it replaces out of the history and is not a firing: nothing that reads the history as firings counts it. PRD 3.13 keeps manual waypoints as a way to force a divergent world back into agreement, and the author-s decision (R) is that the operator should not have to keep any: this is the history the engine keeps for them, and each step is a load-to-time target - before cue 12 is that cue at -1. Appended by the HANDLER of every applied go, cue.fire and trigger.fire, which is what makes it model state a replay reproduces rather than something a hook noticed; never stored, because a history is what the machine happened to be doing (PRD 4.10) and a show reopened tomorrow starts a new one. A load to time RETIMES it (2026-09-19): the steps before the instant move to the clock the rebuilt runs are on, and the steps after it, which the jump undid, go - so what is published is what is in force, and a later aim reads right.

What the next GO on this list carries on (PRD 3.32; Doh!, D2, 2026-10-02): the cue a Doh! paused and the second it carries on from, space-separated - a second of the file for a media cue, the scene-s own second for a scene, and no second for a mic cue, which has no position - or empty when the next GO starts whatever it fires from its top. A cue that had been heard is paused by a Doh! rather than ended, and the next GO on it carries it on from where it was at the press over a tenth of a second. It is dropped by a second Doh! press, any GO on the list, a jump, a fire by name or by a trigger of the cue or of a cue inside the paused scene, a seek of the arm the standby made at the point (which then plays where the hand put it), and the engine-s own reading of the playhead at the press when that finds the file all but over. Written by those handlers, never by a hook; never stored, because it is what the machine is doing (PRD 4.10).

What kind of cue this is, derived from the element rather than stored: a Group is a group and a Media is media. Deriving it is what stops a client turning one kind into another by writing a word, and what lets the grammar refuse a file attribute on a cue that plays nothing.
The decimal cue number. A string, because 12.5.1 is one; mutable, renumbered during tech, and never an identity.
The cue's name, as the operator reads it.

The cue's name for a seven-character display, written by somebody rather than cut by the machine (PRD 3.16: authored short names, never auto-truncation). Empty, a strip display cuts the name to its width and says nothing about it.
Free text for the designer.
Whether the cue runs at all. A disabled cue is skipped, not deleted.
A #RRGGBB decoration. Never the sole carrier of information.
How long after entry before this cue starts. A group has one of its own, and it runs before its members begin their own pre-waits, so raising it defers the whole group.
How long after completion before this cue reports done to its parent. A group is complete once every member is, its members' own post-waits included; the group's post-wait then runs on top of that.
The identifier of the containing list or group.
Position among siblings, zero-based.

Where this cue sits in the thing that contains it: an ordinary member, one of the cues in its group's header or footer, or one of the list's persistent cues. Derived from the element that contains it rather than stored, like `kind` and for the same reason - a client that could write it could move a cue between a group's preparation and its members without the group knowing. A cue at the top level of a list is a member. The whole vocabulary is declared here although `persistent` cannot occur until the section exists, because an enum that grows later grows under a client that has already read it.

Whether an enable or disable cue has switched this cue on or off for this run (namespace draft 27). file means none has, and the cue runs as its enabled says; on and off override enabled until the show is closed or reverted, or loaded to a time, which works it out again from the cues it walks past. Never saved: the show file holds what the designer decided, not where a performance had got to (PRD 4.10).

How far ahead this cue has been got ready, derived from its prepared run. PRD 3.12: preparation is per PARAMETER rather than per cue, so a block that is partly anticipatable says so rather than pretending. Idle is the resting state and means nothing has been prepared, which is not a failure - a MIDI cue can never be prepared and reads idle for ever. Preparing is in progress; pending is waiting for a slot somebody else holds (3.9e, in words rather than colour); partial means something in the block could not be anticipated and will happen at entry; armed means everything that could be prepared was, with nothing to verify; verified means every pre-sent value was read back equal, which is the only one of the six that says the desk agrees.

The ancestor group whose header prepares this cue, or empty for the ordinary case - prepared with its own group, as everything is. THE MARK IS THE DECISION AND THE HEADER LINE IS A READING OF IT (PRD 4.10): nothing is copied into the Header element, so editing the line is editing the member, deleting the member removes the line with no repair rule to write, and the two can never come to disagree because there is only one of them. It names an ANCESTOR rather than being a tickbox, because a cue three groups deep can be got ready by its own group, by the act, or by the opening scene, and which one is a decision about how early. A value naming a group that is not an ancestor is a validate warning and is ignored - not a refusal, because the repair is somebody dragging it somewhere sensible and yesterday-s show must still open.

The media to play, as a path relative to the bundle's media/ folder. Relative because a show travels between machines and an absolute path is a fact about the machine it was authored on. A file that is missing is reported when the show loads and fails the cue when it is armed - it never fails the load, because a show with one missing sound is still a show somebody has to run tonight.

The level the cue plays at, as decided. Not what it is doing: a fade writes run/<id>/level and leaves this alone, so the document keeps saying what somebody chose while the run says what is happening. -120 dB is silence rather than a very small number.
How far into the file playback begins. A cue that starts at the downbeat rather than at the top of the recording.

The speed the cue plays at, as decided (namespace draft §22): one is the file's own, a half takes twice as long, two takes half; up to twenty. Nought holds the file where it is - silent in varispeed, a stopped tape, and a held sound in timestretch (decision DR). Heard while the cue sounds: an edit reaches a playing run on the next tick, placed a launch horizon ahead as a launch is, unless a speed fade holds that run. What rateMode says a speed other than one does to the pitch. Rests at one (PRD 4.6). Below nought the file plays BACKWARDS at that speed's size (namespace draft 41, WX, the author's pick): a fade from one to minus one stops the sound and plays it back, turning round where it crossed nought; a cue launched at a negative speed plays its piece - its ranges, or its start offset to its end - from the end back to the start.

What a speed other than one does (namespace draft §22): varispeed moves the pitch with it, as a tape does; timestretch keeps the pitch where it was recorded and changes only how long the sound takes. Read when the cue is armed, because a mode is on Tracktion's rebuild list - a change reaches the next GO, never a sounding cue (DV). Timestretch goes through Signalsmith's stretcher even at one, because the operator chose it.

How many channels the file has, decided when it was imported and written into the cue rather than read off the disk whenever it is wanted. The file travels between machines and may be absent tonight, and the routing below is shaped by this number - a cue whose count nobody knows cannot be pointed at an output without guessing what a guess would cost. Nought means nobody has said, which is every show written before the number existed.

A volume curve over the file, as (seconds, level) pairs: seconds of the FILE from its start, not of the cue from its GO, and a level in dB within the -120..12 the cue level may take. An OFFSET on the cue level - one more term beside a fade, a hand on a strip and a DCA - so nought is the cue as written. Straight in dB between two points; before the first it holds the first, after the last the last. It follows the file wherever it plays: the start offset, a jump, a scrub, and every pass of a looping range, which hears the same stretch of it again. Empty, the default, is no lane (namespace draft 20).

The movie this sound is locked to, by identifier, or empty (namespace draft 37.5, WJ and WL, the author's): a movie's own sound, imported beside it. While it names a video cue, the sound fires, stops and is taken back with that movie, on the same sample, and its start offset, speed and Ranges are the movie's - copied in the same edit as every change to the movie's, and refused here as locked-to-movie. Everything else is the sound's own, as any media cue's. Empty is detached; naming a cue that is gone is detached too, until an undo brings the movie back.

Retired 2026-10-08 and read by nothing: it asked for a two-channel file to be folded onto a mono output, each side at half, and without it the run failed. The routing now folds a stereo cue onto any one-channel output by itself (namespace draft 42), so the switch had only an error left to choose. Kept so a show that set it still opens; no window offers it.

The direct out this cue-s channels land on, by identifier; empty routes it nowhere by this road and is what every cue starts as. A mono cue feeds every channel of a stereo out; a stereo cue onto a mono out is folded, each side at half (2026-10-08); any other cue wider than its out fails the run as bad-route, because which side a third channel belongs to is a layout somebody has to say. Chosen among the outputs whose kind is direct - a mix channel is reached through a Send, at a level, which is the whole difference between the two.

This cue is MEANT to share its direct out with another. PRD 3.9c-s -allow marking deliberate sharing-, as feed/shared already gives a processor slot: the live-range analysis is conservative by design and reports overlaps it cannot prove impossible, so this is how a designer says of one pair that they considered it. It silences that pair-s warning and NOTHING ELSE - the menu still marks the out as taken, because which outs carry sound is a fact and the warning is a complaint, and only a complaint can be answered.

The DCA this cue is assigned to, by identifier, or empty. A mark on the member and never a list on the DCA (PRD 3.28), so assigning eight cues is a multi-select edit and nothing flows downward (4.12). Adds that DCA's trim, and the trim of every DCA it sits inside, to the level of every run of this cue - level only, one to one in dB; a mapping per assignment comes later.

sampler member: the strip this clip is played from, by identifier - a fader or a pad (author, 2026-09-25: 'I need to specify which track goes where'). Empty is automatic: the next sampler strip nobody in the group has named, in member order, which is how every member was placed before. Two members naming one strip: the first in member order has it and the other is placed automatically. A strip that is not a sampler strip of this layout - deleted, or made a DCA strip - is no pin at all, and the member is placed automatically rather than left silent.

sampler member: the strip it is played from under the rule strip describes - its own, or the one automatic placement gives it - and empty when the layout has none left. Derived, so the menu says the strip that will be armed and never a guess at it.

sampler member: what the cue list put on each strip before this member's group, as strip and cue pairs - for every strip an earlier sampler group in the same list used, the member that group placed there, the nearest one winning. List order is the order a show runs in, so this is what a choice replaces (author, 2026-09-25: 'it should state what is the previous assignment in chronological order of the cuelist unless it's free'). A strip missing from it is free.

sampler member: what letting go does. hold stops the clip on release - a pad lifted, a touched fader let go at silence - after the short releaseFade, so it does not click; playOut lets it run to its end, and silence on the fader is a mute rather than a stop.

sampler member, play-out only: what a press does while the clip is already playing. restart takes it from the top; noop leaves it alone; stop ends it with the release fade. A hold clip cannot be pressed again by the hand holding it, and a press from anywhere else is ignored while it is held (PRD 3.8, 3.27).

sampler member: whether the velocity of a press sets the level the clip starts at (author, 2026-09-23). Off, a press starts at the member's initialLevel, which is where its fader already is. On, a press at 127 starts at 0 dB and a press at one at velocityFloor, in a straight line between them in dB.
sampler member: the trim a press of velocity one starts at when velocity is on, and where a pressure of one takes it when pressure is on. -40 dB is a light tap on most pads; -120 is silence.

sampler member: whether pressure on the pad - polyphonic aftertouch or channel pressure - rides the clip's trim while it is held, on velocity's scale: 127 is 0 dB, one is velocityFloor, and nought is ignored so a pad that rests at nought after the hit does not pull the sound down. A pad is a fader without a motor (author, 2026-09-23), and this is that fader.
sampler member: how long the fade to silence takes when a hold clip is released, or a play-out clip is stopped by a second press. Fifty milliseconds reads as a stop and does not click.

sampler member: the level its strip's fader flies to when it is armed on one, and the trim the clip starts at (author, 2026-09-23). The fader waits there, and a touch on it starts the clip at wherever the fader is by then. A trim on the cue's own level, as every fader is (PRD 3.9a), so nought - the default - plays the clip at the level it was written at. On a pad it is the level a press without velocity starts at.

Whether the EQ of this cue is in the signal at all. Off, every band is skipped and the audio passes untouched - the A/B a designer reaches for. On with every band flat is the same sound and the same bytes, by construction.

Whether the high-pass is in. A flag rather than a frequency parked at the band edge, because the click of a rotary switches a filter in and out, and a click that moved a frequency would move it somewhere.
Where the high-pass turns over: second-order Butterworth, -3 dB here and 12 dB an octave below. 80 Hz takes the rumble out of a voice.
Whether the low-pass is in. As eqHpf.
Where the low-pass turns over, second-order. 12 kHz takes the hiss off a recording without dulling it.

Whether band one is in the signal. Off takes the band out and keeps its shape, frequency, gain and width, so switching it back on brings back the same band - the press of its gain rotary on a surface page (author, 2026-09-25). A switch rather than the gain parked at nought, for the reason eqHpf gives: a press that moved a number would move it somewhere, and the number is what somebody decided.
What band one is: a peak, or a shelf that lifts or drops everything below its frequency. The low band is the one that wants to be a shelf.
The centre of band one, or the corner of its shelf.
The gain of band one. Nought is the band out of the signal, which is what every band starts at and rests at (PRD 4.6): a peak at nought is no peak.
The width of band one: higher is narrower. 0.7 is a gentle bell, 5 is a notch. On a shelf it sets how steep the corner is.

Whether band two is in the signal. Off takes the band out and keeps its shape, frequency, gain and width, so switching it back on brings back the same band - the press of its gain rotary on a surface page (author, 2026-09-25).
The centre of band two. Always a peak.
The gain of band two; nought is out.
The width of band two.

Whether band three is in the signal. Off takes the band out and keeps its shape, frequency, gain and width, so switching it back on brings back the same band - the press of its gain rotary on a surface page (author, 2026-09-25).
The centre of band three. Always a peak.
The gain of band three; nought is out.
The width of band three.

Whether band four is in the signal. Off takes the band out and keeps its shape, frequency, gain and width, so switching it back on brings back the same band - the press of its gain rotary on a surface page (author, 2026-09-25).
What band four is: a peak, or a shelf over everything above its frequency. The high band is the one that wants to be a shelf.
The centre of band four, or the corner of its shelf.
The gain of band four; nought is out.
The width of band four, or the steepness of its shelf.
The ids of this cue-s enabled Fx children in chain order, space-separated - which inserts the cue has, in the order they process, for a page that walks them (pages draft 8, item 3).

The names of this cue-s EQ rows a locked show is riding live, space-separated, empty when none is (author, 2026-09-25). Under the lock EQ and sends are ridden like faders: heard at once, written to nothing, until the show is unlocked and somebody keeps or discards them. The rows themselves publish the value heard.

The identifiers of this cue-s sends, space-separated: its Send children in document order, then any a locked show made live - the index a page or a surface walks rather than scanning every send in the tree (2026-09-25).

How long the file is, in seconds, read from its header once when the show is opened. On owner `media` and not `cue`, or every memo, group and fade would grow one - and `fade` and `stop` already carry a duration of their own, which is a different thing entirely. A READOUT about a file rather than a decision anybody took, so it is never stored (PRD 4.10) and never logged. Nought means the file is missing, unreadable, or in a format this build has no reader for; the state solver reads that as -I do not know how long this is- and says so rather than guessing.

The SHA-256 of this media cue's file as the analyser read it, in sixty-four lower-case hex characters: the key its pyramid is served under, at /media/<hash>/timbre on the same port, so a client that wants the colours of a bar asks for them by this and never by a path. The file this cue names NOW: a run armed before its cue's file was edited, or one still sounding after its cue was deleted, keeps playing the file it was armed with, which this does not follow. Empty until the analyser has hashed the file AND built its pyramid, so a hash a client can read is one the route will answer. Published from the runtime half although it is about a file, because it arrives late and changes while the show does not - the cached half would freeze it at whatever it was when a cue was last edited. On owner `media` for `duration`'s reason: a memo has no file to hash. A READOUT about a file and never a decision, so it is never stored (PRD 4.10) and never logged.

Which direct outs are PROVABLY carrying another cue while this one plays, as bus and cue pairs - at most one pair per output, naming the nearest cue that is in the way. What the direct-out menu marks as taken. Proven means one of two things and nothing else: the other cue never ends on its own, or both cues sit inside one timeline or automatic chain where the seconds are exact. Everything a GO separates is in outsMaybe instead, because between one GO and the next there is a person and a person is not a duration.

Which direct outs MIGHT be carrying another cue while this one plays, in the same pairs. The menu marks these with no word at all rather than with a guess (author, 2026-09-22: -when uncertain, cue playing out until its end, then just don-t mark it, the user will decide-). A finite cue at the top of a manual list may well have finished long before the next GO, and it may equally still be sounding; nothing in the document says which, and saying so is more use than picking one.

How wide the cue is after the inserts it switches in (2026-09-26): its file's width, or wider where a plugin made it so - a mono cue through a stereo reverb is two. What its routing reads: where it is sent somewhere with room for every side it plays them apart, and where there is room for fewer they are summed. Its file's width when no insert widens it.
How many samples late the cue sounds through the inserts that take it, as their plugins declare it - never compensated: PDC is off and a cue is not started early for it. Nought with none in.

The named input this cue takes, by identifier - Voix solo, not input 3 (PRD 3.18, namespace draft 18.2). Empty takes nothing, and is what a new mic cue starts as. An input its channel cannot take fails the run in words, and wfg validate says so before the show.

The rack channel it plays through, by identifier: the channel's plugins, EQ and output are the cue's for as long as it holds the channel (decision BX). A cue wanting a channel another holds waits for it and says so. Empty plays through nothing, and wfg validate says so.
How long GO takes to bring it from silence to its level. Nought opens it at once, behind a click-free ramp (namespace draft 18.5).

On a sampling channel (Phase 9c, decision CF): what GO does with a take the channel already holds. wait leaves it silent until Rec or Loop - the default, which makes no sound nobody asked for; loop plays it from the in point, and with no take waits for Rec; clear empties the channel for a fresh take. A later cue on the channel finding the take of an earlier one is how scene 5 brings back the loop of scene 2.

On a sampling channel (Phase 9c, namespace draft 19.3): whether the channel sounds its input as well as its loop, while it records and while it loops. Off by default: the voice being sampled is usually heard through the desk already, and would otherwise double.

The identifier of the bus this destination feeds. A destination names a bus and never a hardware channel: the bus is where the author said a channel exists, and a show moved to a different rig re-points buses rather than every cue.

The coefficients from the cue's channels to the bus's, row by row: input 0 to every bus channel, then input 1, and so on. Its length is the cue's channel count times the bus width, and a length that does not match is refused when the show loads rather than discovered mid-cue. A coefficient is a plain multiplier and carries no dB - level is the cue's, and this is where it goes.

The cue this range belongs to, derived from where it sits. A range is a child of the media cue whose file it cuts up (PRD 3.24), so this is the containment read back rather than a second copy of it that could disagree.

Where it sits in the cue's list of ranges, counting from nought. Derived, and the one thing about a range that IS positional: the ranges of a cue are a playlist and a playlist is an order. It is read-only for the reason a cue's index is - moving a range is object.move, an edit somebody made, not a number somebody wrote.
What the strip shows (PRD 3.24). A range is a region of a file that somebody named - the verse, the approach, the last eight bars - and the name is the only part of it a designer says out loud.

Where in the file the range begins, in seconds. Ranges may be discontiguous and in any file order (author, 2026-09-06): a media cue with ranges is a playlist over one file, so the second range may start before the first ends, or before it begins.

Where in the file it ends, in seconds. Checked against the file length when the cue is ARMED, which is when the file is read, and not when the show loads - a show whose media is not on this machine yet is still a show somebody has to open. An out that is not after its in fails the arm.

How many passes of this range before playback continues into the next. Nought is for ever, which is what an ambience bed is: it plays until something advances it. The count is of passes rather than of repeats, so one is the range played once.

Whether the range BOUNCES between its points (namespace draft 41, the author's ping-pong loop): out to its out-point and back to its in-point, each way a pass, rather than from its in-point again. Played backwards, it bounces the same way round.

The cue this trigger fires, derived from where it sits. A trigger is a child of the cue it belongs to (PRD 3.7), so this is the containment read back rather than a second copy of it that could disagree.

What kind of thing fires it. The three inputs Phase 3 builds: a message on Go.dot own OSC port, a MIDI event on an input it was told to open, and a time of day. Timecode is Phase 10, and GO is not in this list at all - GO is the operator, and the only trigger that moves the standby (PRD 3.5).
Whether it can fire. A trigger turned off during tech is still written down, which is the whole difference between disabling one and deleting it.

osc: the address that fires this cue, arriving on Go.dot own OSC port over UDP. Refused at load if it falls under /godot or under a mount prefix, because those are NODES - a trigger there would be a message that both wrote a value and fired a cue, and nobody could tell which had been meant.

osc: an argument the message must also carry, written the way the log writes one - f:1, i:3, T, s:go. Empty matches any arguments including none, which is what a bare address means to most of the things that will be sending one.

midi: the declared port the event must arrive on, by identifier. Empty is any input, which is what a rig with one MIDI cable wants. THE PORT AND NOT THE CABLE (2026-09-22): the show says "Lights" and the machine says which socket that is, so moving an interface changes one binding in the settings and every trigger that named the port goes on firing. Matching a device name here would mean editing every trigger in the show for a moved cable, which is the cost the port exists to avoid.
midi: the channel, 1 to 16. Nought is any, and it is nought rather than -1 because MIDI channels are one-based everywhere a musician looks at them.
midi: the event type. Four of them, which are the four a surface sends: the rest of the event types exist for MIDI CUES (PRD 3.10) rather than for listening.
midi: the note, controller or program number.
midi: the velocity or value that must match, or -1 for any. A note-on with velocity nought is a note-off on a great many devices, so matching on it is a thing somebody will need to do deliberately.

clock: a local time of day, HH:MM:SS, fired once each day it is crossed while the show is open. The wall clock is the one input the model refuses to read - nothing inside the engine reads a clock, which is what makes a replay reproducible - so a crossing is noticed outside it and arrives as a logged command like any other.

The cue whose sound this fade moves. It targets the CUE and finds its live run when it fires, because a cue is what somebody wrote down and a run is what happens to be playing - and the show has to say the first without knowing the second.

Whether the fade moves its target's level (namespace draft §22.6). On, so every fade written before a fade could move a speed moves the level it always did; off, the fade leaves the level alone and moves only what rateOn asks for. QLab's shape: a switch per thing a fade moves.

Where the fade ends, in dB. -120 is silence rather than a very small number, and it is the default because a fade to silence is what most fades are - a fresh fade cue is a slow cut to nothing, which is a real thing to want and can only ever make the show quieter. Not read while points holds a curve, whose last level is where that fade ends.

Whether the fade moves its target's speed, to its rate (namespace draft §22.6). Off unless asked. A switch rather than an empty rate, because an unreadable number reads as nought in places, and nought is a speed: a stopped tape. A speed fade aimed at a group, a DCA or a mic cue moves nothing, and wfg validate says so (EC).

The speed a fade with rateOn takes its target to, over its duration and along its curve - straight or S-shaped in the ratio itself, since nought has no logarithm (EA). One is the file's own speed; nought is a tape stop in varispeed and a held sound in timestretch. The drawn points stay the level's. Below nought the target plays backwards (namespace draft 41): a fade through nought turns the sound round where it crosses it.
How long it takes. Zero is a jump, and it is the default so that a fade nobody has finished writing does something obvious rather than something slow and mysterious.

The shape it takes between the two levels. Linear in the dB domain, which is what a fader feels like; sCurve eases out of the start and into the end, for a fade that should not announce itself. The two shapes a fade has when nobody has drawn one: not read while points holds a curve, because two shapes multiplied together would be a third that nobody drew.

A curve somebody drew, as (t, level) pairs: t a fraction of the duration and level in dB, within the -120..12 a fade's level may take. The fade meets each breakpoint at its time and runs straight in dB between them, which is what linear already means. Empty, the default, means curve applies - so a fade written before there was anything to draw with goes on meaning what it meant. Where it holds a curve it is the whole of the shape, and its last level is where the fade ends. The fade leaves from wherever the run's level is rather than from the first breakpoint's, for the reason a fade over a fade does: anything else is a jump, and a jump on a PA is a click. Refused, when written and when the show loads, unless it is pairs whose times climb strictly from exactly 0 to exactly 1.

Whether the target's run is stopped when the fade arrives, at whatever level it arrives at. Off, a fade to silence leaves the run playing silently until it ends by itself, which is what a fade that will come back up wants; on, the arrival is the stop, the same path a stop cue's fade verb takes.

The DCA whose trim this fade moves, by identifier, instead of a cue's level. When it is set, target is not read: a DCA has no run to find, so the fade moves /godot/dca/<id>/trim from wherever it stands to level, and stopWhenDone means nothing. A second row rather than a wider target, because target names a cue and the refers check knows one kind per row.

The target's sends this fade moves, as bus:dB pairs space-separated, sorted by bus (namespace draft §26, OY). A bus listed is moved to its level over the duration and along the curve, straight in dB; a bus not listed is left alone, which is what unticking it in the fade's mixer does. Keyed by the bus rather than by the target's Send, so a retargeted fade moves the same mix: one the target has no send into is faded in from silence as a send of the run alone, and one it has switched off stays off (PB). The run's, never the cue's: the cue's own send is untouched (OZ).

The target's EQ numbers this fade moves, as row:value pairs space-separated - eqHpfFreq, eqLpfFreq and each band's Freq, Gain and Q, in the rows' own units and ranges (namespace draft §26, OY). A gain moves straight in dB, a frequency and a Q straight in their logarithm (PA). Switches and shapes are not listed: a fade is a move between two numbers, and a switch has no middle. Empty moves nothing.

The target's plugin values this fade moves, as plugin/index:value pairs space-separated, the plugin named by its set entry and each value normalised 0..1 as the plugin takes it (namespace draft §26, OY). Moved straight in the 0..1. A plugin the target has not switched in has its value moved and not heard. Never a whole state: a fade holds values (PH).

What the fade moves a video cue to, as row:value pairs space-separated, sorted - opacity, scale, offsetX, offsetY and rotation, and a movie's rate, in the rows' own units (namespace draft 36, VS). Each moves from where the picture is to its value over the duration, along the curve; a row not listed is left where it is. stopWhenDone takes the picture away where the fade arrives.
The cue this stops. As with a fade it names the cue and finds the run, and a target that is not running is a no-op that is applied rather than refused.

How it stops. Hard stops now and takes Tracktion's own click suppression with it; fade runs a fade to silence first and stops when it arrives. The verb is separate from the duration so that a stop with a duration nobody meant cannot become a slow one by accident. afterMember and afterIteration are the two GRACEFUL ones, and they are only meaningful against a group: they let the scene reach a boundary it was going to reach anyway - the end of the member playing now, or the end of this round - and stop there, which is how an infinite loop is left without a cut. Against anything else they are a hard stop, because there is no boundary to wait for. advance is the third graceful one and belongs to a ranged media cue (PRD 3.24): it lets the range playing now finish the pass it is on and then leaves it, either into the next range or into silence - which is how an infinite ambience is got out of without a cut. Against a cue with no ranges it is a hard stop, for the same reason: there is no boundary. record, loop, overdub and clear are not stops at all (Phase 9c, namespace draft 19.6): aimed at a sounding mic cue on a sampling channel they are the press of that name on its take - Rec, Loop, a layer begun or closed, the channel emptied - and against anything else they are applied and do nothing, as a stop aimed at a cue that is not running is. enable, disable and jump are not stops either (namespace draft 27): enable and disable switch the target on or off FOR THIS RUN - the show file is never written, reopening the show forgets it, and Doh! of the GO puts it back - and jump moves the standby pointer of this cue's own list onto the target, firing it too when andGo is on.

With the jump verb: once standby is on the target, the target is fired as GO would fire it, and standby moves past it. The fire belongs to the GO that fired this cue, so one Doh! takes back both and puts standby back here (namespace draft 27). Ignored by every other verb.

Which slice of the target to go to, by identifier, when the verb is advance - and empty, which is what advance has always meant, is the NEXT one. Naming a slice is how a bed is sent to its outro from wherever it has got to rather than stepped through everything in between, which on a loop that never ends is the difference between a gesture and a wait. The slice still finishes the pass it is on before the jump, because that is what makes an advance graceful; a slice of some other cue is a warning and the run goes to the next one instead.

The cue this starts when it fires - by name, as cue.fire does, so standby does not move and the target may sit anywhere in any list. A start cue is a memo that presses a button (2026-09-19): it fires, its run is done the next tick, and the target runs on its own. What the live recorder writes into a take: one start cue per cue the operator fired, at the second they fired it, so a night pressed by hand can be played back by a timeline. A target that is a manual group is refused when it fires, as cue.fire refuses it.
How long the fade half takes, when the verb is fade. Ignored by a hard stop.
The shape of that fade. Ignored by a hard stop.

The node this cue writes, which is an address in a mounted namespace rather than a message somebody composed. Naming the NODE is what lets the tree check it: a cue pointing at something the target does not have is findable before the show rather than during it, and the node already says what type it takes.

What to write, spelled the way the log spells an argument - f:0.5 for a float, i:3 for an integer, T for true - and a LIST of them, space-separated, for a message of several arguments (namespace draft 45): /adm/obj/1/xyz takes f:0.5 f:2 f:1.2, and a device that describes the node takes exactly as many as it declares, each coerced to its own type. Empty sends the message with no argument at all, which is what /go is to a great many desks. The type is in the text so that a cue meaning the float and a cue meaning the integer are different cues rather than the same cue read twice by two machines.

How long the cue takes to be done. None finishes as soon as it is fired; sent finishes when the datagram has left the socket; verified finishes when the target has been asked and has answered with the value that was written. A sequence of verified cues is a chain that waits for each device instead of hoping (PRD 3.11), and it is the only one of the three that can tell you the device disagreed.

How long verified waits for an answer before failing the run. Ignored by the other two waits. Five seconds because it is long enough for a device that is thinking and short enough that a cue which is never going to answer does not hold a show past the point anybody would have given up on it. Zero means the first reply or nothing.

What Doh! does with what this cue sent (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-01: a default per device that can be overridden at cue level). device - the default - follows the Doh! setting of the device its address is under; takeBack puts back what it wrote where it can be read back and has the corrected GO send it again; leave leaves it to the device-s operator - nothing put back, nothing sent again by the corrected GO, which still runs the cue with its timing and sends nothing. Only the exact words override: anything else reads as device. On screen, leave reads Meh and takeBack reads Undo(h) (the author-s words, 2026-10-02); the stored words do not change.

What Doh! sends to take back what this cue sent, when it takes back (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-03: we might send a go back command or a different cue or scene number if for instance the light board has autofollow cues after the last one sent). Written ahead, never at the Doh. The address, a space, then the value spelled as the value row spells it - /lx/go i:11. Empty - the default - follows its device-s rollback, else the previous command: the message of the nearest cue before it in its list that sends to the same device; with none, nothing is sent and the cue is named as could not be taken back. Only what somebody typed is stored. Sent once per device per Doh, the first sent cue-s, in place of could not be taken back; a value the device reads back is still put back exactly; the corrected GO sends the cue again.

The identifiers of the cue-s further messages, in the order they are sent, space-separated (namespace draft 45, YP): the cue-s own address and value are its first message, and each <Message> under it is one more, sent after it in the same tick - in one bundle where its device takes them. Read-only: a message is made with message.create and taken away with object.delete.
The OSC cue this message belongs to, derived from where it sits, as a range-s cue is.
Where it sits among the cue-s further messages, from nought: the cue-s own message goes first, then these in this order. Derived, and counted among messages alone.

The node this message writes, as the cue-s own address is - and under the same device (namespace draft 45, YV, the author-s pick): a cue talks to one device, so its target menu moves every message at once and Doh! keeps its per-device setting. A message under another device fails the run at GO with several-devices, and wfg validate warns of it.
What this message sends, spelled as the cue-s own value: a list of atoms, every argument of the message, empty for one that carries nothing.

The identifier of the declared <Port> this cue sends on. An identifier and not a name, for the reason a route names its bus by one: the name is what a person reads and what --midi-out is given, and renaming a port must not silence every cue that used it. A port that is declared and not bound fails the RUN with no-port and never the load, because which cable "Lights" is on is a fact about the building (PRD 4.10) and a show travels to a rig that has not been patched yet.

Which event to send. Every type PRD 3.10 lists, including sysex, because a show that can send seven of eight is a show somebody has to keep a second program open for. The type decides which of the fields below mean anything, which wfg validate says out loud rather than the grammar refusing - one element per type would be eight elements for one concept.
The channel, one to sixteen. One-based because that is what is written on every device a musician has ever looked at, and unlike a TRIGGER's channel there is no 'any': a message has to go somewhere.

The first byte of the message: the note for a note on, off or aftertouch, the controller for a control change, the program for a program change. Ignored by pitch bend, channel pressure and system exclusive, which have no such thing. NAMED AFTER ITS PLACE IN THE MESSAGE and not after any one of those meanings, because it is all of them depending on the type above it - and a client shows the word that fits, so nobody reads data1 anywhere but in the file. It was called number until 2026-09-22 and could not stay: every cue already has a number, which is its place in the list, and two rows of one name on one element are one attribute doing two jobs - the same twelve read as the cue's number and as the program it sends.

The second byte: the velocity of a note, the value of a control change, the pressure of an aftertouch, or the whole fourteen bits of a pitch bend, where 8192 is the centre. Ignored by a program change, which has only one byte, and by system exclusive. Nought to 127 for everything but the bend. Renamed from data with its partner (2026-09-22) so the two read as the pair they are.

The bytes of a system-exclusive message, in hex, F0 to F7 inclusive - written the way a manual prints them, because that is where a designer is copying from. Ignored by every other type. A dump of any size is legal and the send is off the tick thread for exactly that reason: on Windows a hundred bytes busy-waits the calling thread for about thirty milliseconds.

How long the cue takes to be done. As a network cue, minus verified: MIDI has no read-back, so there is nothing that could answer, and asking for one is refused when the show loads rather than waiting for ever at half past seven. sent says the bytes reached the port.

What Doh! does with what this cue sent (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-01). device - the default - follows its port-s Doh! setting; takeBack has the corrected GO send it again (a MIDI message cannot be put back); leave leaves it to whatever plays on that port - the corrected GO runs the cue with its timing and sends nothing. Only the exact words override: anything else reads as device. On screen, leave reads Meh and takeBack reads Undo(h) (the author-s words, 2026-10-02); the stored words do not change.

What Doh! sends to take back what this cue sent, when it takes back (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-03: we might send a go back command or a different cue or scene number if for instance the light board has autofollow cues after the last one sent). Written ahead, never at the Doh. The type, the channel, then the numbers - programChange 1 11, noteOn 1 60 0, controlChange 1 7 0 - or sysex then its hex bytes, F0 to F7. Empty - the default - follows its device-s rollback, else the previous command: the message of the nearest cue before it in its list that sends to the same device; with none, nothing is sent and the cue is named as could not be taken back. Only what somebody typed is stored. Sent once per device per Doh, the first sent cue-s, in place of could not be taken back; a value the device reads back is still put back exactly; the corrected GO sends the cue again.

What the show calls this port. The document holds what somebody decided (PRD 4.10), so it says 'Lights' or 'The desk'; --midi-out=<name>=<device> is what binds it to a cable on this machine, and the two are separate for the reason a bus and a hardware channel are.

The MIDI output on this machine this port sends through, by the name wfg midi lists. What somebody decided and what reads sensibly at the next venue, which is why it is in the show and not beside it (PRD 4.10); --midi-out overrides it for one session. Empty is unbound, and a cue on an unbound port fails its RUN with no-port and never the load, because a show travels to a rig nobody has patched yet.

The identifier that output had when this machine last found it, tried BEFORE the name. Two things fail in opposite directions and that is why both are kept: an identifier is operating-system formatted and is not stable - on Windows it carries the device's instance path, so moving a cable to another USB socket changes it - while a name survives the move and cannot tell two identical interfaces apart. State rather than show: it is what the machine matched and not what anybody decided, so it never dirties the show, and a stale one at another venue simply fails and falls through to the name. Written back by the engine whenever a port binds by name, so the next start is exact.

The MIDI input this port listens on. Events arriving there are matched as THIS port, so a trigger names the port and never the cable - which is what makes moving an interface one edit instead of one per trigger. Empty listens to nothing; --midi-in overrides.
The identifier that input had when this machine last found it, tried before the name, for the reason the output's twin gives.
Whether events arriving on this port's input fire triggers. Off is a port that sends and does not listen, which is most of them - a lighting desk takes messages and has nothing to say back.

Whether cues on this port are sent. Off, the cue still runs and finishes carrying the warning not-sent, exactly as a network device's tx does, so a rehearsal in a room without the desk plays the show instead of printing a column of failures.

Whether this port plays sound - a synth or a sampler rather than a lighting desk (the author, 2026-10-01: Should we have a toggle for this rather than assume?). A MIDI cue that fired to a port marked so, its tx on, makes its scene heard for Doh!: paused and carried on by the corrected GO, where a scene of lighting cues is taken back exactly and started over. Off unless set; a port marked and not bound on this machine still counts, binding being a fact about the building.

What Doh! does with what a cue sent on this port (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-01: always leave to its operator, unless somebody says otherwise). leave - the default - leaves it to whoever plays that port: nothing sent again by the corrected GO, which runs the cue with its timing and sends nothing, and the Doh names it. takeBack has the corrected GO send it again, since a MIDI message cannot be put back. Only what had already left is concerned; a cue may override it either way. Only the exact word takeBack takes back. On screen, leave reads Meh and takeBack reads Undo(h) (the author-s words, 2026-10-02); the stored words do not change.

A general go-back command for Doh! (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-03: a general go back command overrides at the device level, but can be edited). What a cue sent here that cannot be put back is taken back with this message, under Undo(h), unless the cue has its own; empty - the default - leaves each cue to the previous command. The type, the channel, then the numbers - programChange 1 11 - or sysex then its hex bytes.
Whether this port has a device behind it. What the machine found, not what anybody decided, so it is published and never stored.

Why it has not, in one sentence, and empty when it has: no such device on this machine, or a name that fits two of them and cannot be told apart. Ambiguity is a refusal rather than a guess - a MIDI cue arriving at the wrong desk is worse than one that does not arrive - and this is the sentence that says which.

The MIDI inputs this machine has, one per line. NEWLINE and not space, because a device name contains spaces and nothing else would split - the same argument document/warnings makes. Read when the show opens and again on midi.rescan, never on the tick thread: enumerating MIDI devices blocks for milliseconds on Windows.
The MIDI outputs this machine has, one per line, read the same way.

The identifiers of the runs the engine is publishing, in the order they were created. A finished run keeps its place here for five seconds and is then dropped - Gogo is the present tense (PRD 7), and a four-hour show would otherwise publish four hours of finished runs on every tick.
The cue this run instantiates. A run is the live instance and the cue is what somebody wrote: the cue keeps saying what was decided while the run says what is happening (PRD 4.10).
The kind of the cue this run instantiates, copied at launch so a client reading a run does not have to go and look the cue up - and so the answer survives the cue being edited underneath it.

The group run this one is a member of, or empty at the top of a list. Runs and not cues, because the same cue can be a member of a group that is running twice - a shuffled loop plays it in round three and again in round five - and which one finished has to have an answer.

The runs this group run is organising, in the order they were spawned, space-separated. A group owns time, order and lifetime and no output of its own (PRD 4.12), so this is the whole of what it holds.

Which part of itself a group run is in: its own pre-wait, its header, its members, its footer. A READOUT and never a model input, like `position` and `rangeIteration` - the scheduler holds it on the job and mirrors it here for a client to watch, so it is not written to the log and a replay, which runs no scheduler, leaves it empty. Empty on every run that is not a group. The two prepare values arrive with the horizon (PR 4.5) and are declared here so the enum does not grow under a client that has already read it.

Where the run is. Preparing means the horizon reached it and it is getting ready ahead of any GO - a run in that state is NOT live, and nothing that asks whether a cue is running counts it (PRD 3.12). Waiting means its pre-wait is running and nothing has fired yet; armed means its track is held and its media is being made ready; playing means the launch has been placed; stopping means a stop was asked for and has not landed; postWait means its own work is over and it is holding before it reports done to whatever is waiting on it; done and failed are both finished, and a failed run says why in error.

The track it plays on, or -1 before one is held and after it is given back. The track count is the polyphony ceiling, so this is also which of those voices it is using. A playing track is never stolen.

How far into the RUN it has got - which is how far into the FILE when there is one, start offset and range wrap included, and simply how long it has been going for a run with no voice at all. A fade is the case that makes the difference worth stating: it has a duration the document declares and nothing placed on a track, so it is measured in ticks from the GO that started it rather than in samples from a launch that never happened. Nought until it is launched, for every kind, because a cue parked on a standby has not got anywhere yet. A READOUT and never a model input: it is published for a client to watch and is not written to the log, because a log of every position would be a log of the clock rather than of anything anybody decided.

The tick GO was applied on for this run, which is when it STARTED - and nought while it has not, which is every run the anticipation window has prepared and nobody has let go yet. A tick index and not a wall clock, because the engine's own notion of when is the tick and a wall clock in a published node would be a value a replay could not reproduce - the argument undoName already makes. It exists so that a running pane can be ordered the way the show happened rather than the way the run table happens to hold it: a cue prepared ahead of time is created BEFORE things that are already sounding, so the engine order puts the next cue above them, which is upside down from where an operator looks for it. Ordered by this, with the not-yet-started last, a pane reads top to bottom like the list it came from.

How many seconds of the wait it is in are left, counting down to nought - and nought whenever it is not waiting at all, so a reader never has to ask a second node whether this one means anything. It is the pre-wait while the state is waiting and the post-wait while it is postWait, which are the two states a run can be counted down in; both are the SAME question from where an operator sits - how long until this does the next thing - and telling them apart is what the state node is for. Computed from the absolute tick the wait comes due at, which a command handler set from its own tick, so it is exact rather than accumulated and a client that missed twenty publishes still reads the truth on the next one. A client draws it as a bar that EMPTIES rather than one that fills: what somebody watching a wait wants is the time left, not the fraction served. The total it is a fraction OF is the cue's own preWait or postWait, which is in the document where decisions live and not repeated here.

What it sounds like where it has got to, as three numbers: the hue in degrees, then the saturation and the lightness from nought to one, of the analysis frame at its current `position` (PRD 3.30). Empty until the analyser has a pyramid for its file, and a client draws its own grey for empty - 3.30's answer for a clip whose colours have not arrived. `0 0 0` is silence, and a real reading rather than a missing one: lightness nought is below the ramp's darkest, so it cannot be mistaken for a low sound. A READOUT computed when the tree is published, like `position`, and never logged. The rate cap of 10 is what a surface is told to draw it at (PRD 3.30); the engine recomputes it every tick like everything else.

How loud the file is where the run has got to: the analysed peak of the frame at its position, in decibels below full scale, to a tenth - -120 for a silent frame - or empty until the file is analysed, as timbre is. Before the fader and the DCA: it is the sound's own shape, which a surface pulses its colour with - half its level over a few seconds, half how it moves (author, 2026-09-25: 'make part of the LED level match the long term level of the music and the other half the shorter term variations').

What a picture run shows, as one colour: the average of its layer over its canvas, as #RRGGBB, its opacity and its DCA already in it - dark when it is see-through (namespace draft §38, WR). Read by the renderer from the frames it holds, ten times a second, through the compositor the no-window probe uses; empty while no renderer runs or for a run that is not a picture. What a DCA strip-s ring shows of its pictures.
The level it is playing at now, which is what a fade writes. Not the cue's authored level - that one stays where the designer left it, so a night of riding faders does not rewrite the show.

The speed it is playing at now, which is what a speed fade writes and what the playhead advances by (namespace draft §22). Not the cue's authored rate - that one stays where the designer left it, so a night of speed fades does not rewrite the show. One for every run that is not a media cue. Negative while the file plays backwards (namespace draft 41).

How many blocks the launch was late by, when GO arrived before the arm had finished. Zero is the ordinary case, and the number is here because it is the difference between GO is instant as a claim and as a measurement.

Which of the cue's ranges is playing, counting from nought, or -1 for a run that is not in one - every kind but media, and a media cue with no ranges. A TRANSITION IS AN EVENT (PRD 3.15): this changes when the boundary into the range is PLACED, which is a logged command, so a replay reproduces which range every run was in at every tick with no audio at all.

Which pass of that range is playing, counting from one, or nought when there is no range. A READOUT and not an event, like position: it is computed from the sample counter rather than logged, because a bed looping for four hours would otherwise write a record every few seconds for something nobody decided. It is the 3 of the strip's 3/8.
Which round this group run is on, counting from one. Zero before the first round has been drawn. A client showing 3/8 is showing this and iterations.
How many rounds this run will play, copied from the group when it started - so an edit to loops changes the next run and not this one. Zero means for ever.

The cue identifiers of the round in progress, in the order they will play, space-separated. MATERIALISED rather than computed: a shuffled round is drawn once, written into the log, and read back from there on replay - which is what lets a session reproduce without the random number generator ever being consulted again.

The members dropped from this run, space-separated. Pruning is RUN-LOCAL and evaporates with the run (PRD 3.6): it is what an operator does at 22:40 when one of eight ambiences is wrong tonight, and it must not be an edit to the show - tomorrow the cue is back.

The seed this run is drawing its rounds from: the group seed when there is one, and a fresh one otherwise. Published because a shuffled night somebody liked is a night worth being able to ask for again.
