Why it failed, when it did: no-track when every voice was busy, media-missing when the file is not in the bundle, is there and is not audio, or a range is not inside it, no-port when a MIDI cue names a port nothing was bound to, bad-message when its own fields do not make a message anybody could send, no-slot when the cue has more ranges than the graph has launcher slots - which is a range added since the show was loaded, and needs a reload rather than an edit - bad-route when the destination cannot be honoured, bad-target when a fade or a stop names a cue this show does not contain at all - which is different from one that is not running, and is a warning wfg validate has already given, send-failed when a message could not be put on the wire, and the write refusals - bad-address, read-only, type-mismatch - when a network cue names a node the target does not have or will not take. timeout when a verified cue asked and nothing answered in time, and disagreed when something answered with a different value, which is the one failure that means the device is there and is not doing what it was told. For a mic cue (Phase 9b): no-input when it takes no named input, bad-channel when it plays through no rack channel or a shared one, bad-width when its input is not as wide as its channel takes, not-built when the channel was declared since the graph was built and waits for Load now. Empty otherwise. A failed run was still an APPLIED command - the request was legal and the show could not honour it, which is a different thing from a request that was malformed.

The slots this run holds, by identifier, space-separated. A VOICE IS NOT AMONG THEM - a track is not a declared object and where a voice is held is this run-s own `track`. Held from the arm until the run reaches done or failed, which is the same moment the voice is freed: `holdsTrack()` is a track and an unfinished run, so the claim-s release and the voice-s are one rule written in two places rather than two rules (PRD 3.9e).

The slots this run has claimed and not yet been given, because something else is holding them. PRD 3.9e: a claim on a busy slot is neither a failure nor a race - it lands when the holder-s run ends, and the claimant shows PENDING meanwhile. GO has already returned (4.1). A holder that never ends on its own, an infinite loop, is the operator-s to end. It also holds the word voice for a sampler member armed onto a strip while every track was busy (decision Z, 2026-09-23): that claim waits too, and lands when a track frees. The launch waits on this being empty: half a cue is not a cue, and sending it into a slot somebody else holds is the fighting a claim exists to prevent.

Something this run did less of than it meant to, while still going. NOT a weaker `error`: an error is a run that did not do what it said, and a warning is a run that carried on. `no-channel` is a cue that lost an exclusive rack channel and played dry, which PRD 3.9e calls DEGRADE and which is the whole point of that policy - reporting it as a failure would either stop the scene or teach an operator to ignore the state that means stopped. not-sent is a cue aimed at a device whose tx is off, or a MIDI cue on a port whose tx is off: it ran, it was applied, and nothing left the machine. left-to-operator is a cue a corrected GO ran without sending, because the GO that Doh! took back had already sent it to a device left to its operator (PRD 3.32). In words, never colour alone (4.8).

Whether this run was started by the persistent assertion (PRD 3.29) rather than by a person or a group: the engine found the cue not as its section declares - a bed whose file had run out, a value the desk no longer held - and put it back through run.assert, after an applied trigger and never on its own clock. Shown so an operator can tell a sound they started from one the machine restored.

The trim a hand is adding to this run's level, in dB - the fader or the pad on the strip the run holds, and nothing else writes it. Added to the cue's own level and to every trim above it. A run armed onto a strip starts at its cue's initialLevel - where the fader flies to and waits for the touch that starts the clip - and so does a run armed onto a pad. Written with node.set by a surface, a panel or the page, and a ride is not undoable, being nothing anybody decided about the show (PRD 4.10).

How loud it left its track over the last tick, in decibels below full scale: the loudest sample the track output stage sent, after the EQ, the inserts, the level and the trim of the hand - so after the fader - or -120 while it has no voice sounding (author, 2026-09-25: 'On the sampler fader displays of the D700 can we have a post fader level meter too?'). A surface draws it on the strip that holds the run. A READOUT like position, taken from the audio side once a tick and never logged: a replay, which has no audio, reads silence.
The strip this run holds, by identifier, when it is a sampler member on one; empty otherwise. The strip's holder read from the run's side, so a running pane can say which fader a sound is under.

Whether a pad is down on this run - pressed and not yet released. While it is held a press from any other origin is a no-op, and so is that origin's release (PRD 3.27): the hand that started it owns it.

Whether this sampler clip is soloed on its strip (author, 2026-09-25: 'The solo switch could be engaged on a track to prevent other faders in the bank to trigger'): while it holds, a press on any other strip of its bank - a touch, a pad, a fire by name - starts nothing. Set with run.solo, the SOLO button on a surface; it lets go by itself when the clip stops - its end, a stop, a kill or a release - so a solo left on never outlives the clip it protected. A performance, never an edit: nothing is written to the show.

Whether a run.seek sent now would move this run (K9, 2026-10-02, namespace draft 23.18), so a client offers a scrub exactly where the engine honours one: a media run not over and not taken back by Doh!; a group run the machine paces - a timeline, or a sequence that advances by itself - that the walk times as written, or that has begun a round, a seek then landing within the round it is in. Never a manual group (a person stands between its members) or a sampler bank (played by hand). A readout, mirrored every tick and never logged.

Where the round a running scene is in began, in seconds of the scene's own clock as position reads them (2026-10-05, namespace draft 30.6): for a group run a run.seek would move now, the round the seek is held to (K9) - a looping or shuffled scene's current round, or the one round of a scene that plays once, begun when its pre-wait ended. Nought for every other run. A client draws the scene's strip from here to here plus roundLength and keeps a scrub inside it. A readout, solved by a hook once a round and never logged.

How long the round in roundFrom is, in seconds: the furthest end among its members and the wait after it, as the seek clamps it (namespace draft 30.6). Nought when it cannot be solved - a member whose length is not known, a range that plays for ever - or when the run is not one a seek would move; a client then falls back to its own gearing. A readout, solved by a hook once a round and never logged.
The identifiers of the group's children, in order, space-separated.

The cues in this group's header, in order, space-separated. A header runs before the group's members (PRD 3.6) and is an ordinary cue list, so this is the same kind of answer as order - about a different list.

The cues in this group's footer, in order, space-separated. A footer runs at group exit and BLOCKS: the group is not done until its cues are, so a following scene that reallocates the same channels waits for the release rather than racing it.

The identifier of this group's header section, or empty when it has none - what object.move and cue.create take as a parent to put a cue in it. Made by group.role, which answers with the one that exists. Published (2026-09-18) so a client can move a cue into a section it can see, rather than into a container it has to guess.

The identifier of this group's footer section, or empty when it has none - what object.move and cue.create take as a parent to put a cue in it. Made by group.role, which answers with the one that exists.

The cues whose preset names this group, in document order, space-separated - the header lines somebody did not write. Derived the way order and headerOrder are, and run BEFORE the written header cues when the horizon reaches the group: a written header cue may reasonably depend on what the presets set - position the source, then move it - and the reverse dependency has no natural example. What the horizon does with a preset member is its preparable part and nothing else (PRD 3.12); the member still runs where it sits, at its own moment, in its own group, which adopts the arm the ancestor made rather than making a second one.

Whether the group is drawn shut, its members hidden under its row. State, not show: how a group is read is not a decision about what it plays, so it lands in state.xml and does not mark the show unsaved.
Whether the group's header band is drawn shut. State, as `folded` is.
Whether the group's footer band is drawn shut. State, as `folded` is.

Whether members are scheduled at entry, run one after another, or wait for a hand. sampler launches none of its members: GO arms the group, every member is loaded onto a strip, and faders and pads start them - in any order, any number of times, several at once (PRD 3.27).
Whether a member starts when the previous completes or on GO.

How the members of a round are ordered. sequential plays them as they are written; shuffle draws a fresh order for each round, redrawing until the first of the new round differs from the last of the one before it - so a member is never heard twice running across a boundary. With two members that constraint decides the order completely, which is correct rather than a degenerate case: alternating is what a designer asking for two shuffled ambiences means.

How many ROUNDS this group plays before it is done. Rounds, not playbacks: with play set, a round is a subset of the members, and three loops of two-of-five is six cues rather than three. Zero means for ever, which is what an ambience bed is, and is left by a stop verb, an advance or run.stop rather than by counting.

How many members a round plays, out of however many there are (PRD 3.6 play N of M). Zero means all of them, which is the ordinary group. Larger than the membership is the same as all of them rather than a refusal: a designer deleting a member should not have their show stop loading.

The seed a shuffled group draws its rounds from. Zero means a fresh one per run, drawn when the run starts and written into its log - so a shuffled show is different every night AND every night reproduces exactly. A seed set here is the other thing somebody wants: the same order at every performance, which is how a shuffled scene gets rehearsed.

sampler: what arming this group does to the sampler groups already armed (PRD 3.27). group closes every other sampler group - each launches nothing new, plays out what is playing and hands each strip over as that clip ends; strip takes only the strips this group's members land on and leaves the rest to whoever had them, and a group that has lost every strip completes. Read when the group is armed and at each refresh.
The DCA this group is assigned to, by identifier, or empty. Adds the DCA's trim to the group run's own, which reaches every member through the sum a group already is (PRD 3.6, 3.28).

The address this device answers at, and the root every cue aimed at it carries. SEVERAL, separated by spaces, for a device whose addresses start at the root of its own world: a DiGiCo S21 reached directly answers at /channel for every strip control, /console for ping, pong and the channel counts, and /digico for snapshot recall, so its row reads "/channel /console /digico". Declaring it three times would be three rows, three names and three sent counts for one console, and giving it one root that is not its own would mean the address in the cue is not the address in the manual somebody copied it from. A space is what separates them because an OSC address can never contain one, and a device with a single root reads exactly as it always did. A device that DESCRIBES itself has one: its namespace file is one tree and mounts in one place. EDITING THIS DOES NOT REWRITE THE CUES: a cue holds the whole address it writes, so a root somebody changes leaves every cue under the old one aiming at nothing, which wfg validate says out loud. Moving a cue from one device to another is the target menu's job.

How the mounted target is reached. Only udp carries messages today; tcp and ws are declared because a document should be able to say what a device is before Go.dot can talk to it, and a mount declaring either is refused when the show loads rather than going quiet during it.

Where the target is. A literal address rather than a name, because a socket resolves a hostname on every send whose destination differs from the last one, and a blocking lookup on the tick thread is a frame nobody gets back. It defaults to this machine because the ordinary rig is Go.dot and its processors on one box; anything else says so.

The port the target listens on. Required, and deliberately without a default for the same reason audio/tracks is: no number could be right for every device, and a mount that guessed would send into the dark and report success. UDP never tells you nobody was listening, so this one has to be right in the document or it is never right at all.

The bundle-relative OSCQuery namespace file describing the target, and EMPTY is the ordinary case for a device somebody typed an address into. Empty declares an OPAQUE device: nothing is published under its prefix, a cue aimed under it is sent exactly as it was written with no coercion and no read-back, and a cue whose wait is verified is refused when the show loads because there is nothing there to ask. A described device is the other half of PRD 3.22 and is unchanged: its nodes are checked, typed and askable.
Default outbound rate cap for the mounted nodes.
Whether the mounted nodes may be pre-sent before GO. False for third parties.
Default resting state for the mounted nodes.
Whether the namespace file has been read.
How many nodes the mount contributed.

The port the target answers OSCQuery on, which is a different number from the one it listens for messages on - WFS-DIY takes messages on 8000 and describes itself on 5005. Zero means it was not declared, which is the only honest default: most devices do not run an OSCQuery server at all.

Whether this target can be ASKED what a value is, and how. Transport says how to send and says nothing about the other direction, so without this a cue whose wait is verified against a write-only device is a cue that can never succeed and nothing notices until the show. None is the default because it is true of most devices: OSCQuery was never standardised, and a mounted namespace is usually hand-written for a box that will never answer. A verified cue aimed at a none is refused when the show loads, which is the whole point of declaring it.

How many messages have left for this target since the show opened. A readout for a tech rehearsal, and the first thing to establish when a device is not moving and nobody knows whose end is wrong: UDP cannot report delivery, so what Go.dot can honestly say is how many times it sent.

What the show calls this device - 'Lighting desk', 'The WFS' - which is what a target menu shows and what somebody reads in a list. The prefix stays the address: a name is for people and renaming one must not move a single cue, which is the reason a MIDI port has both too. Empty shows the prefix instead, so a device is never a blank row.

Whether what this device sends is accepted. It is read today by one thing only: with strict senders on, a datagram from a host no declared device holds with rx set is dropped and logged rather than obeyed. What is DONE with what a device sends - a state machine watching it, a desk writing cues into the show - comes later, and the flag is stored now because it is a decision about the rig rather than a thing the machine noticed (PRD 4.10).

Whether cues aimed at this device are put on the wire. Off, the cue still runs and still lands in the tree and the log - it finishes at once carrying the warning not-sent - so a rehearsal in a room without the desk plays the show instead of printing a column of failures. On is the default because a device somebody declared is a device they mean to talk to.

Whether everything Go.dot sends this device in one tick leaves as one OSC bundle (namespace draft 45, YQ, the author-s pick: the device-s setting rather than the cue-s). On, a cue-s messages and every curve moving at that moment arrive together - a source-s x, y and z in one datagram, even from two cues - time-tagged immediately, a datagram closed at 1200 bytes and a message too big for one sent alone. Off - the default, and what Go.dot always did - each message is a datagram of its own, which every device reads; a device that cannot read a bundle ignores one in silence, so it stays off until somebody knows.

What Doh! does with what a cue sent to this device (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-01: on a lighting desk running sequences, fixing with Doh would really do more damage than the light operator handling the damage). leave - the default for every device, whatever its kind, Go.dot-s own processors included (confirmed by the author, 2026-10-02) - leaves it to the device-s operator: nothing put back, nothing sent again by the corrected GO, which still runs the cue with its timing and sends nothing, and the Doh names the device and the cue. takeBack puts back what a cue wrote where the device can be read back, and has the corrected GO send the cue again. Only what had already left for the device is concerned, and a cue may override it either way. Only the exact word takeBack takes back. On screen, leave reads Meh and takeBack reads Undo(h) (the author-s words, 2026-10-02); the stored words do not change.

A general go-back command for Doh! (PRD 3.32; the author, 2026-10-03: a general go back command overrides at the device level, but can be edited). What a cue sent here that cannot be put back is taken back with this message, under Undo(h), unless the cue has its own; empty - the default - leaves each cue to the previous command. The address, a space, then the value spelled as a cue-s value row spells it - /lx/key/go_back I.

Why the engine cannot use this device as it is declared - no usable port, a namespace file it could not read, a transport it cannot speak - in one sentence, and empty when it can. It exists because these refusals were a line on somebody's terminal at startup and nothing else: a device that will never work looked exactly like one that works, in every client, until a cue failed during the show.

Whether messages are taken only from the devices this show declares. On, a datagram whose sender is not a declared device with rx set is dropped and written to the log as a refusal naming who sent it; off, which is the default and what Go.dot has always done, anybody who can reach the port is heard. It gates the OSC port alone: a client on the WebSocket is a client rather than a device, and gating those would lock the page and the tablet out of their own engine.

How many datagrams strict senders has dropped since the show opened. The first thing to look at when a surface has gone quiet and nobody knows whose end is wrong: a number that climbs as somebody presses a button says the message is arriving and being refused, which is a different morning from one that never came.

How many cues can sound at once - the fixed number of audio tracks, and so the polyphony ceiling. Zero is legal and means a show with no audio. Required, and deliberately without a default: the number is a decision about the shape of a show, and no value here could be right for every rig. WRITABLE since 2026-09-21, because a decision a client cannot state is a decision nobody can take: it was read-only, no command set it, and a show made by File - New therefore declared nought and could never play anything. The graph is built from it when the audio settings are applied, so a change lands at the next apply and not under a running show - which is the same moment a changed buffer size lands.

How many channels one track carries, and so the widest cue this show can play. Two is a stereo file, which is what almost every show is; a six-channel bed or a first-order ambisonic one needs it said. A cue wider than this fails its arm as bad-route rather than being quietly narrowed - PRD 3.9b: width is explicit and never automatic. Fixed when the graph is built and never after, like tracks and for the same reason (3.25), so a show is reopened to change it. It costs: every track carries this many buffers whether a cue uses them or not.
The audio device the engine has open, or empty when there is none.
Open the saved audio interface when this show starts.
Audio driver type selected for this show.
Output interface selected for this show. Empty selects the system default.
Input interface selected for this show. Empty disables inputs.
Requested buffer size. Zero uses the device default; the granted size is observed.
Space-separated hardware input indices per logical input. Zero based; -1 disconnects. Empty preserves identity routing.
Space-separated hardware output indices per logical output. Zero based; -1 disconnects. Empty preserves identity routing.

Whether the output patch has stopped following the output layout one for one. False in a fresh show: the patch stays empty, which the device layer already reads as identity, so every output added, removed, moved or widened simply re-flows it and the designer never touches a matrix. It goes true when somebody edits the patch by hand, and when the first media run launches with audio - after which every output keeps the interface channels it has and a new one takes the next free ones. State rather than show: it records what has happened to this rig, not a decision about what the show plays, so it lands in state.xml beside the standby and does not mark the show unsaved.

Whether the input patch has stopped following the list of named inputs one for one - the twin of patchSettled, for the other side of the interface. False in a fresh show: the input patch stays empty, which the device layer reads as identity, so every input added, removed, moved or widened re-flows it. True once somebody edits the input patch by hand, after which every named input keeps the interface channels it has and a new one takes the next free ones. State rather than show, for the reason patchSettled gives.
Whether the requested audio settings have finished applying.
Number of completed audio settings apply operations in this session.
Why the most recent audio settings operation failed.
The observed device sample rate.
The buffer size granted by the device.
Space-separated buffer sizes supported by the active interface. Read from the engine-owned device without opening another driver.
Output test signal: off pink noise tone sweep or pulse.
Hardware output under test. Minus one means stopped.
Output test sine frequency.
Output test level.
Output test hold toggle.
The number of active hardware input channels.
The number of active hardware output channels.

The interface input delay as its driver reports it, read when the device opens and carried on the logged audio.settingsReady so a replay reads what the session read. Nought for the hosted interface, which has no converters. Half of what a mic cue is late by before any plugin (PRD 3.18).
The interface output delay as its driver reports it, read and carried as inputLatency is. The other half of what a mic cue is late by before any plugin.

How much delay the plugins of a mic cue may add, in milliseconds, before the cue, its channel and the plugin that did it say so (PRD 3.18, decision BY). Never refused and never compensated: a budget is a line drawn, and crossing it is said in words.

How long Esc takes, in seconds (author, 2026-09-28: a Panic fade duration that fades out all playing cues). Esc and the PANIC button fade every cue that is sounding to silence over this long and then stop it; a group-s footer runs when its members have gone, as PRD 4.4 has it. A mic cue is faded at its input and its reverb rings on. A cue already fading out on a stop of its own keeps that stop when it lands first. Esc again within the double-press window cuts everything at once, fade or not. Nought is a cut. Read at the press, so a change lands at the next Esc.
How many hardware output channels are available to route to. A cue wider than this is refused when the show loads.

The show-s mix channels by identifier, space-separated, in the order the outputs list them - by first channel, then identifier: what a surface-s Send page walks, one rotary a channel, in the order the window-s send mixer draws them (2026-09-25).
Whether audio is running. An unlocked device is present and producing nothing, which is a different failure from no device at all and wants a different remedy.

What came of the last time the interface came back from an outage on another clock and the show followed it (PRD 6.2, 2026-09-28), in words: from which rate to which, and whether the cues that were playing were stopped. Empty until it first happens this session.
The tick at which the show last followed the interface onto another clock, so a client can tell rateMoved from a refusal that came before or after it. Nought until it first happens.
The bus name as the designer wrote it. Names are what appear in a dropdown and on a scribble strip; channel numbers are not.

Whether this bus is a direct out - where one cue's own channels land, chosen from that cue's direct-out menu - or a mix channel that many cues send into at a level. The word decides which menu the bus appears in and nothing about the hardware: both kinds are contiguous output channels and both are summing points, so a second cue sent to a direct out is mixed there like anywhere else rather than refused.

The first hardware output channel this bus occupies, counting from zero. Read-only at the door and maintained by bus.create, bus.delete, bus.move and bus.width, which repack every bus as the running sum of the widths before it: a client that could write this one could leave two buses overlapping, and nothing downstream would notice until a show night. A layout written by hand that is not packed is left exactly as it is and warned about, never rewritten.

How many consecutive channels the bus occupies - one for a mono output, two for a stereo pair, more for a processor send. Explicit and never inferred: the engine will not quietly widen or narrow a cue to make it fit. Read-only at the door and changed by bus.width, which repacks the channels after it.

A level trim on everything leaving this output, in dB, after every cue and send has reached it (namespace draft §38, the author-s request of 2026-10-07): the place an output is set against the room and the rest of the rig, written in the show because somebody decided it. Nought, the resting value, leaves the output as it was. Applied on the audio side as one gain per channel, smoothed over 20 ms, so a change is never a click; a double Esc leaves it where it is, as it leaves a DCA.

The DCA this output is assigned to, by identifier, or empty (namespace draft §38). The DCA-s trim, and that of every DCA it sits inside, is added to the output-s own trim. It COUNTS AT EACH PLACE (WQ, the author-s pick): a cue marked with the same DCA and played through this output is trimmed by it twice, as a channel and the master it feeds are on a desk with one VCA on both.

The live ranges of this direct out, as cue pairs: the cue that lands on it and the cue whose row that claim is released at, space-separated, one pair after another. Exactly as slot/usage reads, over the same analysis - PRD 3.9c asks for ONE allocator over three resource kinds, and an output channel is the third. Empty for a mix channel, always: many cues arriving at one mix is what a mix is for, so nothing about it is a claim.

The pairs of cues that can both be on this direct out at once, space-separated. A WARNING AND NEVER A REFUSAL (PRD 3.9c) and never a reason to refuse an assignment: two cues on one output sum, which is better than a cue that plays nowhere. Marking either cue-s sharedOut says the sharing was meant and silences that pair - and leaves the menu still marking the out as taken, because which outs carry sound is a fact and only the complaint about it can be answered.

What the flipped fader of this mix rides, while the faders are flipped to a cue: the cue-s send into this mix at its written level plus its lane, or silence when the cue does not send here, where the file is - and, once this lane is armed and touched in a pass, the hand-s level, held after the hand lets go and written into the send-s lane as the difference from its written level. A mix with no send ridden in a pass is given one when the pass ends. Written by the fader through node.set, never a step of undo, and ignored unless this lane records (namespace draft 34).

The identifiers of the named inputs of the show, space-separated, in the order the list reads them - by first logical input, then identifier: what every input menu offers, in the order the interface is wired.

What the input is called - Voix solo - in every menu that offers one. PRD 3.9b: names appear in a dropdown and on a scribble strip, channel numbers do not, because an input number is a fact about a patch that will change.

How many consecutive logical inputs it takes: one for a microphone, two for a stereo line. Read-only at the door and changed by input.width, which repacks the inputs after it, exactly as bus.width does for the outputs.

Its first logical input, counting from zero: the running sum of the widths before it, maintained by input.create, input.delete, input.move and input.width as a bus first channel is by the bus commands. The input patch maps logical inputs to the channels of the interface.

The loudest sample on any of its channels over the last tick, in decibels below full scale, whether or not anything listens to it - the soundcheck question, whether the microphone is alive before GO. -120 while nothing arrives.
Why it is not reaching Go.dot, in one sentence: no input interface is open, or the input lies past the last channel the interface gives. Empty when it arrives.

Every slot the show declares, in document order: the processor inputs of every mount, then the rack channels, then the strips of every surface (Phase 6). A VOICE IS NOT IN IT - a track is not an object anybody wrote down, it has no identifier, and Show/Audio/@tracks is a count rather than a list; where a voice is held has been readable at /godot/run/<id>/track since Phase 2. The allocator still treats a track as a slot kind (PRD 3.9e); being one mechanism does not oblige it to be one data structure.

What the designer called it. PRD 3.9b: the names appear in the dropdown and on the OLED, and the channel numbers do not - -Voix solo- is what somebody wrote down and -input 3- is a fact about a patch that will change.

Which kind of slot this is, derived from the element rather than stored: a Slot under a Mount is a processor input, a Channel under the Rack is a rack channel, and a Strip under a Surface is a strip - the fourth kind, a fader or a pad (PRD 3.9e, 3.16). Derived for the reason cue/kind is - a client that could write it could turn one into the other by writing a word, and the two are released and refused by different policies (PRD 3.9e).

The run holding this slot, or empty. Read off the run table rather than kept beside it, the way a busy track is: a second copy of who holds what is a second thing to keep in step, and the one that is wrong is always the copy.

The runs waiting for this slot, in the order they claimed it. A QUEUE rather than a set, so that who gets it next is read rather than inferred - and the answer is the same on a replay, because the order runs were created in is the order the log made them.

The live ranges of this slot, as cue pairs: the cue that claims it and the cue whose row the claim is released at, space-separated, one pair after another. The data behind PRD 3.9c-s usage-over-show-time plot, which Phase 5 draws. Read in list order rather than in seconds because a manual list has no time between GOs; inside a timeline or an automatic chain the analysis knows the seconds too and uses them to decide overlap, but a pair of cues is what a plot can draw and a person can read.

The pairs of cues whose live ranges intersect on this slot, space-separated. A WARNING AND NEVER A REFUSAL (PRD 3.9c): the analysis is conservative by design - it reports overlap it cannot prove impossible - so a show with an ambience looping for ever and two cues on one processor input reports an overlap that is correct, unavoidable and completely fine. Marking either cue-s Feed or Insert shared says the sharing was meant and silences that pair.

The address of the input this slot is, under its own mount-s prefix: /wfs/input/3 and not input 3. The parameters underneath it - a position, a send, an LFO rate - are ordinary mounted nodes that an osc cue writes; this says which of them belong to the source a cue claims, which is what stops two cues fighting over one trajectory (PRD 3.9b).

How many channels the input takes. Explicit and never inferred, like a bus-s: PRD 3.9b refuses a silent downmix or upmix, and a slot is the one destination where width is enforced, because a slot has one and a bus is a summing point that does not care.

The bus that carries audio into this input. A slot is a routing and a claim in one object: the audio reaches the processor through an ordinary bus, and the claim is what keeps a second cue out of the position and the LFO state behind it. Two separate objects would let a show route a cue somewhere it had not claimed.

Where in that bus this slot-s channels begin, counting from zero. The attribute that makes one wide send ordinary: a rig feeding a twelve-input processor has one twelve-channel bus rather than twelve buses, and the third input is channel two of it. Exactly bus/firstChannel-s idea one level down. firstChannel + width must fit inside the bus, checked when the show loads.

What this channel takes in and puts out. Stereo-to-mono is deliberately absent (PRD 3.18) and wider comes later. The class is the type a claim is matched against, the way a processor input-s width is.

Whether a cue holds this channel alone. A per-source insert is exclusive and is allocated; a reverb many cues send into is SHARED, which PRD 3.9e says is a bus with a chain rather than a slot - declared and published here, and never claimed.

The plugins of this channel chain, by id, space-separated, in the order they process - the order of the Plugin children, which is the order of the track the graph builds for the channel. What a mic cue through the channel switches in and sets (PRD 3.18, decision BX).

What the chain declares with every plugin in, in samples - the worst case, shown when somebody adds a plugin rather than discovered on the night. A mic cue is late only by what it switches in (namespace draft 18.7).

The longest take this channel records, in seconds (Phase 9c, namespace draft 19.2): above nought the channel carries a recorder between its plugins before it and after it, and nought is no recorder - the channel of 9b. What it costs is memory, set aside and touched when the graph is built, never when Rec is pressed: (1 + layers) times this, at the rate, two channels, four bytes a sample. A change takes effect at Load now, and empties the take the channel held.

How many passes the recorder keeps on top of the take, each undoable one at a time (decision CA). A channel that has used them all refuses another pass, in words, until one is undone or the take cleared. Part of the memory the take sets aside; a change takes effect at Load now.

What the graph has set aside for this channel's take tonight, in megabytes - nought with no recorder, or before a graph is built. It moves at Load now, not when takeSeconds or layers do, which is how the Rack tab knows a change is still waiting.
The last thing the take did by itself or refused, in a sentence - the take was cleared because the rate or its size changed at Load now. Empty when there is nothing to say.

What the take is doing, in a word (Phase 9c, namespace draft 19.3): empty; recording its first pass; looping; overdubbing, a layer being laid while it loops; or held, a take kept silent - its cue ended, or GO said wait. It moves with the take verbs and with what the audio thread reports, never with anything the channel happens to be sounding.
How long the take is, in seconds, as the audio thread closed it - a Rec pressed, or the take reaching its longest. Nought while it records its first pass and when it is empty.
How many layers lie on the take, the one being laid not counted. Undo takes the top one off, never the take.
Where the loop is playing, in seconds into the take - for the picture and the running pane, read off the audio side a tick at a time. Not in the log: a replay has no audio and reads nought.

Where the loop starts, in seconds into the take (decision CQ): tonight's, never the show's, answered in front of the document by the take's door, logged as the node.set it is, never a step of the history and allowed under the lock. Kept inside the take and at least two crossfades before the out point; set to the take's start each time a take closes. The loop plays on through every move.
Where the loop ends and wraps to the in point, crossfaded, in seconds into the take - the in point's partner, by the same door and the same rules; set to the take's end each time a take closes.

Whether a Keep is writing this channel's take into the show's media now (Phase 9c, namespace draft 19.8). While it is, Undo and Clear and another Keep are refused busy, so the file is the take that was asked for.

The file the last Keep wrote, relative to the show's media - takes/Looper take 3.wav - or empty. Named by the writer, which found it free on the disk, and logged with take.kept so a replay reads the same name.

The processor input this cue feeds. A cue-s destinations are a list, not a choice (PRD 3.9b): a source into WFS plus a stereo feed to foldback is ordinary, so a Feed sits beside a Route rather than instead of one.

The coefficients from the cue-s channels to the slot-s, row by row, exactly as a route-s are. Its length is the cue-s channel count times the slot-s width, and a length that does not match is refused when the show loads. Required rather than defaulted to an identity: PRD 3.9b says width is explicit and never automatic, and what keeps that from being tedious is copy-assignment and multi-select edit rather than a default that is right until it is not.

This cue is MEANT to share the slot with another. PRD 3.9c-s -allow marking deliberate sharing-: the live-range analysis is conservative by design and reports overlaps it cannot prove impossible, so this is how a designer says of one pair that they considered it. It silences that pair-s warning and nothing else.

The cue this destination belongs to, derived from where it sits. A Feed is addressed by identity like every other object (§1), so this is how a client that found one gets back to the cue that owns it - the same answer range/cue gives.
The mix channel this send feeds. One Send per bus per cue: a second naming the same one is refused when it is created, because two sends into one mix are a level nobody can read off a fader.

How loud this cue arrives at that mix channel, on top of the cue-s own level - so a fade on the cue moves every send with it, which is what a designer means by fading a cue. -120 dB is silence rather than a very small number: a send at silence contributes no coefficient at all, and a track with nothing to add costs nothing to mix.

Whether this send is in the mix. Off contributes nothing and keeps its level, so switching it back on brings back the same send - the press of its rotary on a surface page (author, 2026-09-25). Unlike a send at silence, an off send still says what level it would arrive at.

A curve over the file that this send follows, as (seconds, level) pairs: seconds of the FILE from its start, as the cue's own levelLane, and a level in dB within -120..12. An OFFSET on this send's level - beside what the lock is riding and what a fade moved it to tonight - so nought is the send as written, and the other sends and the cue's level are untouched. Straight in dB between two points; before the first it holds the first, after the last the last; every pass of a looping range hears the same stretch of it again. A media cue's send only: a mic cue has no file to follow. Empty, the default, is no lane (namespace draft 28).
Whether a locked show is riding this send live - its level or its switch held in place of the saved one, or the whole send made under the lock and not in the show yet (author, 2026-09-25).
The cue this send belongs to, derived from where it sits. As feed/cue.

Which entry of the show-s set this cue switches in, by the entry-s id - the id and not the scan-s identifier, because a set may hold one plugin twice and a cue must say which. One Fx per entry per cue: a second naming the same one is refused when it is created, because an entry is on the voice once.

Whether the plugin is in this cue-s signal. Off keeps the values and takes the plugin out - the click that switches an insert in and out on a page - and costs the voice nothing: a proxy that is off is never signalled.

The parameter values this cue sets, as index:value pairs space-separated, each value normalised 0..1 as the plugin takes it, and only the parameters somebody changed: one absent rests at the set entry-s preset. Writable whole for a script; a hand writes ONE parameter through the p<n> nodes beneath, one node a parameter, so a rotary-s turn is one address and one undo step (PRD 4.10).

The whole state of the plugin for this cue, as a file under the plugins/ folder of the bundle, by name - state/ then the entry-s id and the start of a hash of the bytes - or empty for the preset of the entry. What the own window of the plugin changes that is not a parameter (an impulse response, a sample, a mode) is kept here, captured by the editing helper a moment after the hand stops (author, 2026-09-25); it is loaded onto the voice when the cue is armed, before it may launch, and values sit on top of it. Files are never changed once written, so undo points the row back at an older one. A file and not the bytes, for the reason media/file is.
The cue this insert belongs to, derived. As send/cue.
The plugin-s name, read off the set entry, so a page can say which insert it is on without a second lookup.
Where the plugin sits in the chain, from nought: its position in plugins/order, which is the order every voice processes in, whatever order this cue-s Fx children sit in.

Why this insert, switched in, plays its cue dry, in one sentence - the cue wider than the plugin takes, or the plugin would give it back narrower - and empty when it takes the cue (2026-09-26). Never half the cue wet and half dry.

The parameters a locked show is riding live on this insert, by index, space-separated, empty when none is (2026-09-26, the FX page). As media/live: heard at once, written to nothing, until the show is unlocked and somebody keeps or discards them. The values row and the p<n> nodes publish the values heard.

The rack channel this cue processes through. In Phase 4 the claim is bookkeeping and changes no sound: the pool and its claims are this phase-s, and the tracks, the sends and the plugins inside a channel are Phase 9-s (PRD 3.18).
As feed/shared, for an exclusive channel two cues are meant to share.
The cue this insert belongs to, derived. As feed/cue.

The identifiers of the surfaces the show declares, in document order, space-separated. The order matters: a sampler group fills the sampler strips of every surface counted in this order and then by each strip's index, left to right.

The media cue a surface-s rotaries edit on its EQ and Send pages, by identifier, or empty. One cue for every surface, set by surface.aim - a SELECT on a sample strip, or a click on a running cue-s name in the window (author, 2026-09-25). Not the window-s pick and not the list GO acts on: picking a row in the cue list does not move it. Empty when the cue it named is gone. What the hands are on tonight, so never stored (PRD 4.10).

The number the master dial of the control surfaces turns, by its address, or empty. The last number clicked or touched in the window-s inspector or foot panel, set by surface.dial; it stays on that cue-s row when the pick moves, and the dial-s click lets it go (author, 2026-09-26). Empty when what it named is gone. What the hands are on tonight, so never stored (PRD 4.10).

The media cue the fader surfaces are flipped to, by identifier, or empty: set by lane.arm, which flips every fader surface to the cue-s level and sends, and kept across its passes until lane.free, a lane.arm with nothing, a double Esc, or the lock. Tonight-s, never the show-s (namespace draft 34).

The lanes armed to be written, by key, space-separated: level for the cue-s level lane, and the identifier of each mix whose send lane is armed. Set by lane.rec - a strip-s REC while the faders are flipped - before a pass or during one, and kept across passes until the faders are flipped back (namespace draft 34).
Whether a pass is running: the flipped cue playing with every fader following its lane, and each armed lane-s hand heard and written from its first touch until the pass stops (latch).

What the flipped level fader rides: the cue-s written level plus its lane, where the file is - where it starts, outside a pass - and, once its lane is armed and touched in a pass, the hand-s level, held after the hand lets go and written into the lane as the difference from the written level. Written by the fader through node.set, in front of the document like a trim; never a step of undo, and ignored unless its lane records (namespace draft 34).

What the last pass ended in, for a client to say rather than end in silence: the tick it ended on, its cue, then kept with the points it wrote, the first and last second they span and the lanes it wrote, untouched when nobody rode an armed fader while the cue sounded, locked when the show was locked under the pass and the lanes kept as they were, or dropped when a kill took the pass. Empty until a pass has ended in this session (namespace draft 30.4, 34).
What the show calls this surface - 'The D700', 'Pads by the desk'. A name for people; the profile says what the hardware is.

What kind of surface this is, which decides how its strips are driven and what each one has (PRD 3.16: a device profile is topology plus protocol). virtual is the desktop client's own panel and needs no port; mcu is a Mackie Control unit, eight fader strips per port; d700 is the Asparion D700, Mackie plus its native display, colour and rings, eight strips per port; midiPads is a pad controller sending notes with velocity and pressure. Changing it changes how the strips are driven and leaves the strips as they are.

The declared ports this surface is reached through, by identifier, space-separated, in bank order: the first port carries strips one to eight, the second nine to sixteen. The bank is the port and never the message (docs/D700_CONTROL_GUIDE.md 1.1), which is why this is a list. A virtual surface has none.

The preset the hardware must be set to for this profile to read it - Mackie for the D700 - written down and shown to the operator, never detected: two presets can differ by one button, and a surface cannot be fingerprinted from its traffic (docs/godot-asparion-d700-protocol-0.1.md 5).

Whether the engine drives this surface at all. Off, nothing is sent to it and nothing it sends is heard; its strips still exist and are still filled, so a surface left in the van is still part of the layout the show was written for.
midiPads: the channel the pads send on, one to sixteen, or nought for any.
midiPads: the note the first pad sends; the strips follow it upwards, one note each. 36 is where most pad controllers start.

How many strips this surface has, counted off its Strip children. Read-only because a strip is an object: surface.create makes the ones its profile implies, strip.create adds one, and object.delete takes one away.

Whether the engine is talking to this surface tonight: every port it names is bound, with rx and tx on. A virtual surface is always connected, being the client's own. What the machine found and never what anybody decided, so it is published and never stored.
Why it is not, in one sentence - a port with no device behind it, a port whose rx or tx is off, a profile that names no port - and empty when it is.

The serial the hardware reported when it was asked who it is, and empty until it has answered. Nothing depends on it; it is the one identifier that survives the operating system renumbering the ports.

What this surface-s rotaries are showing: show is its normal page, eq the aimed cue-s EQ, send its send levels (author, 2026-09-25), fx the parameters of its inserts, walked in chain order (2026-09-26), loop the take of the aimed mic cue-s channel - in, out, a slide of both and the cue-s level (Phase 9c). The surface-s own, changed by its EQ, Send, FX, Pan and star buttons and by no command - which page a controller shows is where its hands are looking, like the window-s selection. Published so the window can open the foot panel on the aimed cue while a surface adjusts it.
Which page of that kind the surface shows, from nought: an eight-rotary surface shows the EQ-s higher bands on page one.
How many pages of that kind there are on this surface - the EQ-s sixteen controls on sixteen rotaries are one page, on eight are two; the sends are one a rotary.
The address this surface-s page last wrote, or empty since the page came up: how the window knows the surface is adjusting, and which control it moved.
The surface this strip belongs to, derived from where it sits.
Where it sits on its surface, from nought: fader one is index nought. Derived from the element's position among the surface's strips, as a range's index is.

What this strip is for (PRD 3.9a, 3.27): a sampler strip is filled by whichever sampler group is armed - by the member whose strip row names it, or else automatically in member order across the sampler strips of every surface; a dca strip is pinned to one DCA and never reassigned. The two may be mixed on one surface.
The DCA a dca strip rides, by identifier. Read only when the role is dca; a dca strip naming nothing says unassigned and moves nothing.

What the strip's hand control is (PRD 3.16): absolute is a fader, whose position is the value; gate is a pad, a press and a release with a velocity at the press. Derived from the surface's profile - midiPads strips are gates and every other profile's are faders - and published so a client draws the right thing and the engine knows how a clip on it starts: a touch on a fader, a press on a pad.

The node this strip is riding now: /godot/dca/<id>/trim for a dca strip, /godot/run/<id>/trim for the run holding a sampler strip, and empty when nothing is on it. A surface or a panel writes THIS address with node.set and holds it with node.touch; it changes at every handover, which is how one fader rides a different sound after a bank change.

What the strip is doing, in a word for the display and never colour alone (PRD 4.8): free with nothing on it; dca, or unassigned for a dca strip naming no DCA; armed when the member on it is ready and not yet launched; pending while the member waits for the strip or for a voice; playing; held while a pad is down on it; stopping; closing when the group holding it has been taken over and its clip is finishing; lane while the faders are flipped to a cue and its lane is not armed, rec when it is, off for a send switched off, and recording while it is written in a pass (namespace draft 34).
The member cue on this strip, by identifier - the run holding it, or the first run waiting for it - so a display can show a name and a number. Empty on a dca strip and on a free one.
The identifiers of the DCAs the show declares, in document order, space-separated.
What the DCA is called - 'Band', 'Ambiences', 'Everything' - which is what a client and a wide display show.
The name for a seven-character scribble strip, written by somebody rather than cut by the machine (PRD 3.16). Empty, a display cuts the name to its width.

The DCA this one sits inside, by identifier, or empty at the top. A nested DCA adds its parent's trim to its own (PRD 3.28), so Everything over Band over one guitar is three terms in one sum. A cycle is refused when it is written and when the show loads, because no reading of it says what anything should play at.

The trim this DCA is applying now, in dB, added to the level of every run whose cue is marked with it and of every run under a group so marked. Nought is the resting value and what a show opens with. Never stored: it is what a fader is doing tonight and not a decision about the show (PRD 4.10), which is also why writing it is not undoable. Written with node.set from a strip, a panel or the page, and moved by a fade cue that names this DCA.

Whether the show's set differs from the audio graph playing it - an entry added, taken out or moved since the graph was built (2026-09-26). The graph is fixed when it is built (PRD 3.25), so a changed set sounds as it was until plugin.load rebuilds the graph, which Show settings, Plugins offers as Load now. False when there is no graph to differ from.

The identifiers of the plugins the show declares, in document order, space-separated - which is the ORDER OF THE CHAIN on every voice: the EQ first, then these in this order, then the output stage of the cue. The inserts of a cue process in this order whatever order its Fx children sit in.
What the plugin is called on screen and on a scribble strip - the name the scan gave when it was added, editable since two instances of one plugin in a set want telling apart.

The plugin as the machine knows it: the identifier string of JUCE from the scan, fixed at creation and written only by plugin.create. What this show needs; whether the machine of tonight has it is state.
Which kind of plugin it is, from the scan: VST3 on every platform, LV2 on every platform since 2026-09-26, AU on macOS. JUCE names an AU AudioUnit; the show says AU.
Where the file was on the machine it was added from. A fact about that machine kept for the operator who has to find it on another; the identifier is what a load resolves by.

The preset the plugin is put into when the show opens: a .vstpreset file under the plugins/ folder of the bundle, by name, or empty for the own defaults of the plugin. Applied once per instance in the child; the own values of a cue sit on top of it, so a parameter a cue does not mention rests at the value of this preset. A file and not the bytes, for the reason media/file is.

On a sampling channel's plugin (Phase 9c, decision BZ): before the recorder, and what it does is printed into the take, or after the player, and it is heard as the take loops and can be changed without recording again. After by default, so a plugin on a channel that had no recorder stays where it was heard. On a channel with no recorder, and on the set's plugins, it does nothing. A change takes effect at Load now, as the chain's order does.

What became of it tonight: unloaded before the graph of the show is built and on a machine with no audio; loading while the child brings its instances up; loaded when every voice has one; missing when the scan does not know the identifier; failed when the child died or stopped answering - and then every voice that has it switched in is silent, never dry, and nothing calls it until it is back.

Why it is not loaded, in one sentence - the identifier is not in the scan, the plugin took neither the voice's channels, stereo nor mono on its main buses, the child died after 8 misses, it was added since the audio graph was built - and empty when it is.

How many channels the plugin takes on its main input, as it agreed to be laid out on a voice (2026-09-26): the voice's width, or stereo, or mono, asked in that order. A cue wider than this passes the plugin dry, whole, never half wet. Nought before the child has said.

How many channels the plugin gives back on its main output. A plugin whose outputs are wider than its inputs - one in, two out - makes a mono cue stereo; one that would make a cue narrower than it went in passes it dry. Nought before the child has said.
The two widths in words - stereo in, stereo out; mono in, stereo out - for the Plugins tab and the FX chain. Every other bus the plugin has, a sidechain above all, is fed silence.

The delay the plugin itself declares, uncompensated: the proxy declares none and PDC is off, so a cue through this plugin is late by this many samples while it is enabled, on that voice only. Nought until the child reports it.

How many parameters it has, from the catalogue - the cache from the last time this identifier was loaded on this machine, or the child tonight. Nought when neither has answered; the nodes under param/ count to it.
How long the last whole state of a cue took to load onto a voice of this plugin, in milliseconds: a cue armed at GO rather than in standby is late by about this much. Nought until one has loaded.

Why the last whole state of a cue could not load onto a voice - the file is not in the bundle, the plugin refused it - and then that voice plays the preset with the own values of the cue; empty when it loaded.

What the cue puts on its canvas (namespace draft 35, the author's words): a fill, one flat colour over the whole canvas, sitting behind; a mask, a shape laid over what is under it; a picture, an image file; a movie; a capture, the picture a video input brings in from another program (namespace draft 44, YC). One element for every source (VE), because the canvas, the layer, the opacity and the blend are the same whatever it shows.
The canvas it is laid onto, by identifier. Empty puts it nowhere: the cue runs and shows nothing, and wfg validate says so before the show.

The video input a capture shows, by identifier (namespace draft 44, YC): the picture another program sends, placed, graded, faded and blended as a picture is. Many cues may show one input. Read by nothing but a capture. Not `input`, which is a mic cue's rack input at the same cue address.

The video insert the cue's picture goes through, by identifier, or empty for none (namespace draft 44, YE): the picture after its source and grade, at its own size, sent to another program, and what comes back shown in its place - placed, faded and blended as the cue says (YF). Switched on and off by this row, as a sound switches in a plugin of the set. One cue at a time: of two through one insert the later has it and the other shows black (YG); black too while nothing comes back. Not `insert`, a sound's plugin's.

Where it lies in the canvas's stack: higher is on top, and of two on the same layer the one brought up later (VI). An integer per cue and never the list's order, which changes all through a technical rehearsal and would silently restack the picture (PRD 3.19b).

How it lies on what is under it, in display space (namespace draft 35, VD): normal covers it by its opacity; add adds its light; screen lightens as two projectors on one wall do, never past white; multiply darkens, as a gel does. Each at the layer's opacity.

How solid it is, as decided, in % (the author's unit, namespace draft 36, VR): 100 covers what is under it, nought is not there. Not what it is doing - a fade moves the run and leaves this alone, as a cue's level is left alone.

The DCA this cue is assigned to, by identifier, or empty - a mark on the member as a sound's is (PRD 3.28). The DCA's trim, and the trim of every DCA it sits inside and of every group's above the cue, turn into how solid the picture is (namespace draft 37.5, WE, the author's): nought dB and above is the opacity as it stands, -120 dB is nothing, and between the two the picture follows the show's fader travel - half way up the fader is about half way faded. Never more solid than the cue's own opacity.

The colour of a fill or a mask, as #RRGGBB, which the inspector calls Colour (VG): cue/colour is the cue's tint in the list, and every row of a cue shares its address. Black by default - a mask's usual colour, and a fill of black is the plate that covers what is under it.
How long GO takes to bring it from nothing to its opacity. Nought puts it up on the frame it is due.

A picture's file, as a path relative to the bundle's media/ folder, as a sound's is. Read by the renderer as soon as its cue is the standby; GO only shows it, and a picture not read yet stays black until it is (namespace draft 36, VX). A file that is missing is said when the show loads and leaves the picture black, never the show unopened.

How a picture meets its canvas (VO, the author's three): fit shows the whole picture, its shape kept, with bars where it does not reach; fill covers the canvas, its shape kept, the overflow cropped; stretch covers the canvas and distorts the picture. Scale, offset and the turn apply after.
How large, in % of the fitted size (VQ): 100 is as the fit leaves it. A fade moves it (fade/video pairs).
How far right of the canvas's middle, in % of the canvas's width (VQ): 100 is a whole canvas over. Negative is left. A fade moves it.
How far up from the canvas's middle, in % of the canvas's height (VQ, VT: up is up). Negative is down. A fade moves it.
How far it is turned about its own centre, clockwise, in degrees (VT). A fade moves it, and several turns are a fade's to make.
Mirrored left to right about its own centre, before the turn.
Mirrored top to bottom about its own centre, before the turn.

A movie's speed, as a sound's (namespace draft 37, WA): one is the file's own, a half takes twice as long, two half as long; nought holds the frame. A fade moves it (fade/video pairs). Proposed, waiting for the author. Below nought the movie plays backwards (namespace draft 41, WX); a movie played as a preview through FFmpeg holds its frame instead, since it decodes forwards only.

How far into the movie it begins, in seconds of the file, as a sound's start offset - and like a sound's, refused beside Ranges, which say where it plays instead (namespace draft 37.5, WL). A movie with no Range plays once from here to its end.

How long a movie's file is, in seconds, as a sound's duration: read when the show opens, and by the analyser for a file that arrives later; nought until it is known, and for a fill, a mask or a picture. What a Range's out point is held inside.
A picture's or a movie's contrast about mid-grey, in % (namespace draft 36, VP, VU): 100 changes nothing, nought is flat grey. Applied after the gamma.
How far its colours stand from grey, in %: 100 changes nothing, nought is black and white.
Its gamma: above one brightens the middle tones, below one darkens them; the ends stay where they are. Applied first.
Its colours turned round the colour wheel, in degrees; nought changes nothing.
The luminosity curve, on all three channels, as (in, out) pairs 0..1, straight between; empty is no curve (VU). Applied after the saturation, before each colour's own.
The red channel's curve, after the luminosity curve, as (in, out) pairs 0..1.
The green channel's curve, as (in, out) pairs 0..1.
The blue channel's curve, as (in, out) pairs 0..1.

A mask's outline, as (x, y) corners in 0..1 of the canvas from its top-left corner - x to the right, y down - at most 64, filled even-odd (namespace draft 35, UY, VF). Fewer than three is no shape: nothing is covered, or everything when inverted.
How soft a mask's edge is, in canvas pixels across it; nought is a hard edge.
Whether a mask covers what is outside its outline rather than inside - the spill round a set, with the set left clear.
The identifiers of the show-s cue templates, in document order, space-separated (namespace draft §38): the order the Add menu offers them in.

What the template is called in the Add menu and in Apply template - Voice, Ambience bed, Projection left (namespace draft §38). A template is a set of a cue-s settings kept in the show, a new cue born with them; it never names a file.

What kind of cue the template makes, fixed when it is saved from a cue: a media cue, or a video cue of one source - a movie, a picture, a fill or a mask. The Add menu offers it beside cues of that kind.

What the template carries, as the fragment `cue.pastePart` takes: a <Fragment part="…"> holding a stripped copy of the cue it was saved from (namespace draft §38, WP: everything not bound to the file - level, DCA, routing, colour, EQ, sends, effects, speed, how a sample answers a hand; a picture-s canvas, layer, blend, opacity, geometry, grade and mask). Written by `cueTemplate.create` and `cueTemplate.save`, read by `cueTemplate.apply` and `cue.createFrom`. A template is stamped into a cue, never linked (PRD 4.12): a template saved again changes no cue already made.
The identifiers of the canvases the show declares, in document order, space-separated.
What the canvas is called - Stage, Cyclo - in every menu that offers one. A canvas is the flat picture video cues are laid onto (namespace draft 35, the author's word; a surface in QLab's).
How wide the canvas is, in pixels. The pictures are laid out on it and each output's mapping picks the part it shows.
How high the canvas is, in pixels.

How much of the canvas reaches its outputs, in percent: 100 all of it, nought black (namespace draft §38, WT, proposed). It takes the whole composited picture towards black at once - two layers stacked go down together as one picture, never each turning see-through over the other - after the layers and before each output-s mapping. The canvas-s DCA multiplies it.

The DCA this canvas is assigned to, by identifier, or empty (namespace draft §38, the author-s request of 2026-10-07: a DCA can be set on sound and on pictures, and the balance is the user-s). Its trim, and that of every DCA it sits inside, turns into how much of the canvas shows along the fader-s travel, as a cue-s does (37.5, WE): nothing at -inf, the canvas-s level at 0 dB and above. It counts at each place (WQ): a picture cue marked with the same DCA is taken down by it as well.

What the canvas shows, as one colour: the average of its composite, its level in it, as #RRGGBB (namespace draft §38, WR). Ten times a second, from the renderer; empty while none runs. What a DCA strip-s ring shows of a canvas the DCA rides.
The identifiers of the video outputs the show declares, in document order, space-separated.

The displays this machine has, one per line, by the name the system gives each (VL). NEWLINE and not space, because a display's name contains spaces. Read from the renderer, which is the program that opens them; empty until it has started.
How the program that draws the pictures is (UV): stopped while the show has no output, starting, running, or failed - and then it is started again, and what was up is drawn again (VC).
Why the renderer last failed, in one sentence, and empty when it has not.

Where FFmpeg was found on this machine, or empty: beside Go.dot, where WFG_FFMPEG says, or on the path (namespace draft 37.5, WG). Without it a movie that is not HAP neither previews nor converts, and HAP plays as ever.

The movies asked to be converted to HAP this session (namespace draft 37.6, F.3), one line each: the file as the show names it, then a tab, then waiting, converting, done, failed or cancelled, a tab, how far in %, a tab, and what went wrong when it failed.

Whether the projectors' windows are put away while the show is unlocked, so their displays show the desktop for editing (namespace draft 39). Turned on and off by video.hideProjectors; a locked show shows every projector whatever this says. Tonight's, never stored.

FFmpeg being downloaded into Go.dot's own folder (namespace draft 37.5, WN): empty when nobody asked, else downloading, unpacking, checking, done or failed, a tab, how far in %, a tab, and what went wrong; and a tab and where it comes from.
What the show calls this output - Face, Wings monitor. An output is a display on this machine showing one canvas through its own mapping (namespace draft 35, the author's word).
The canvas it shows, by identifier. Several outputs may show one canvas, each through its own mapping (VA). Empty shows black.

The display on this machine it opens on, by the name the system gives it (VL). What somebody decided and what reads sensibly at the next venue, which is why it is in the show: displayId is what this machine called it.
The identifier that display had when this machine last found it, tried BEFORE the name - the MIDI port's twin rows exactly (port/outputDeviceId).

What the output does with its canvas (namespace draft 44, YA): display shows it on a display of this machine, as every output did; ndi sends it over the network, spout to another program on this Windows machine, syphon to another on this Mac - warped and calibrated as an output is, its display rows read by nothing. A kind this system has not got sends nothing and says so.
The name another program finds a sending output by, and empty for Go.dot and the output's name - Go.dot - Face. Read by nothing on a display.

How many frames a second a sending output sends (namespace draft 44, YJ). One at a display's rate rides that display's refresh; any other keeps its own time. Read by nothing on a display, which is drawn at its own refresh.
Whether the output is opened. Off, the cues still run and this output shows nothing, so a rehearsal in a room without the projector plays the show instead of failing it.
How many control points the output's mesh has across (namespace draft 35, PRD 3.19a): two by two is a corner-pin keystone, more bend the canvas round what is not flat.
How many it has down.

Where each control point of the canvas lands on the display, as (x, y) pairs in 0..1 of the display - x right, y down - row by row from the top-left, meshColumns by meshRows of them. A smooth surface runs through them. Empty, or the wrong count, is the canvas filling the display.

The output's calibration, ASC CDL (VP): slope red green blue, offset red green blue, power red green blue, saturation - ten numbers, in the order a .cdl file lists them. Empty changes nothing. What matches a second projector, or a grey wall, to the first.
Whether a display is behind it tonight. What the machine found, not what anybody decided, so it is published and never stored.

Why it is not, in one sentence, and empty when it is: no such display on this machine, a name that fits two of them, or the renderer not running. Nothing fails because of it: the show runs without this output.

Whether the output shows its test pattern - a white frame and a cross - over whatever is up, to find which projector is which. Turned on and off by videoOutput.identify, which Identify on the Video tab sends; tonight's, never stored.
How many frames the renderer has shown on this output since it opened it - its own count, so a frame's pacing is a number and not something judged by eye.
How many of those were shown later than they were due.
How far, lately, a frame was shown from the moment it was due, in milliseconds.

The identifiers of the zones laid over this output's own canvas, bottom first, space-separated (namespace draft 40, WY, the author's pick): each a further canvas through a warp of its own, drawn in this order over what is under it. Derived from where they sit.
The identifiers of the video inputs the show declares, in document order, space-separated.

The pictures other programs offer this machine now, one per line: the kind (ndi, spout or syphon), a tab, and the name the program sends under (namespace draft 44, YB) - what a video input's sender is picked from. From the renderer, which looks for them; empty until it has started.
What the show calls this input - TouchDesigner, Camera 2 - in every menu that offers one. A video input is a picture another program sends, which a capture cue shows (namespace draft 44, YB).
How the picture arrives: ndi over the network, spout from another program on this Windows machine, syphon from one on this Mac.
The name the other program sends under, as videoInputs/available lists it - for NDI the machine's name and the source's, MACHINE (Source). Empty takes nothing.
Whether Go.dot takes it in. It is connected while declared and enabled, never at GO (namespace draft 44, YD), so a cue showing it shows the latest picture that arrived.
Whether its pictures are arriving tonight. What the machine found, never stored.
How wide the pictures arriving are, nought while none are.
How high they are.
How many arrive a second, lately. A live picture is not on the audio clock (YD): it is shown as it comes.
Why none are arriving, in one sentence, and empty when they are: nothing sending under that name, a kind this system has not got, the NDI runtime not installed, the renderer not running.
The identifiers of the video inserts the show declares, in document order, space-separated.
What the show calls this insert - Kaleidoscope, Key - in the menu a cue picks one from. An insert sends a cue's picture to another program and shows what comes back (namespace draft 44, YE).
How the picture goes and comes back: spout to and from another program on this Windows machine, syphon on this Mac, ndi over the network.
The name the cue's picture is sent under, which the other program takes it in by; empty for Go.dot - insert and the insert's name.
The name the other program sends the picture back under, as videoInput/available lists it.
Whether what comes back is arriving tonight. What the machine found, never stored.
How many pictures come back a second, lately.
How long ago the last picture came back, in seconds: the round trip's delay shows here, and is never made up for (YH).
Why the cue shows black, in one sentence, and empty when it does not: nothing coming back, a kind this system has not got, two cues through the insert at once, the renderer not running.
The output this zone is on, derived from where it sits. A zone is a child of its output, as a range is of its cue.
What the zone is called - Left flat, Floor. Empty reads as its canvas's name.
The canvas the zone shows, by identifier (namespace draft 40, WY). Empty shows nothing. One canvas may be in several zones and on several outputs, each through its own warp.

How the zone lies on what is under it on the output - the output's own canvas and the zones before it - in the layers' four ways (VD): normal covers it by its opacity; add adds it; screen lightens; multiply darkens.
How solid the zone is on the output, in %: 100 covers what is under it by its blend, nought is not there.
How many control points the zone's warp has across: two by two is its four corners, more are the extra splits that bend it.
How many it has down.

Where each control point of the zone's canvas lands on the output, as (x, y) pairs in 0..1 of the display - x right, y down - row by row from the top-left, as the output's own mesh. Empty or the wrong count is the whole output, which is where a new zone starts.
